name: Supertime Clock Multiplexing Circuit V2
status_note: Built and on the bench; on 2026-11-18 it was found stuck in reset with U6 running hot. A full write-up is saved next to the board files.
description: Selects one of 31 clock inputs and sends it to 16 identical outputs that feed the update-clock inputs of the NI cards. Input0 on J1 is the step clock: each rising edge advances a 5-bit counter (two 74HC161), and count n routes Input(n+1) to the outputs through four 74HC151 multiplexers, a 74HC138 that enables one of them, and a 74HC32 OR stage. Count 31 is tied to ground, so that slot is always low; after reset Input1 is selected. Two 74HC244 buffers drive the 16 outputs on J4, each through a series resistor with an optional capacitor to ground. J2 is an active-low reset and J3 is +5 V power. J1 and J4 carry signals on odd pins and ground on every even pin.

issues.title: Reset input is unprotected and has no pull-up
issues.detail: J2 goes straight to the reset pins of both counters. D1 and D2 are not fitted and there is no series resistor or pull-up. Driving J2 from the NI card while the board is unpowered, or hot-plugging it, pushes current through the chips' input diodes. On 2026-11-18 the reset line read 1.5 V instead of 5 V with J2 connected, U6 was hot and the board drew about 200 mA.
issues.evidence: Net Net-(D1-A): J2.1, D1.2, D2.1, U5.1 (~MR), U6.1 (~MR) and nothing else. Bench: 5 V unplugged, 1.5 V plugged, +5V rail present.
issues.fix: Replace U6 and U5. Add about 1 kΩ in series with the reset line, fit Schottky diodes in D1 and D2, and add a 10 kΩ pull-up to +5V. Add footprints for the resistor and pull-up in the next revision.

issues.title: Counter cascade glitches at every 8th step
issues.detail: The upper counter U6 is clocked from U5's Q2 through an inverter, so the high bits change about 30 ns after the low bits. After steps 7 to 8, 15 to 16, 23 to 24 and 31 to 0 the output briefly shows Input1, Input9, Input17 or Input25. If that input is high at that moment, all 16 clock outputs get a spurious pulse.
issues.evidence: U6.2 (CP) on Net-(U6-CP) from U8.2; U8.1 on /CLK0 = U5.12 (Q2). U5.11 (Q3) and U5.15 (TC) unconnected. U7.1 (A0) from U6.14, U7.2 (A1) from U6.13.
issues.fix: Clock U6 from Input0, feed U5 TC into U6 CET, take U7 A0 from U5 Q3 and U7 A1 from U6 Q0. On the existing board this is four lifted pins and four jumpers, listed in the note in the board folder.

issues.title: SOIC-16 footprint on U1-U7 does not fit the common package
issues.detail: The footprint is the 4.55 x 10.3 mm SOIC-16 with pads from 2.45 to 4.05 mm off centre. A standard narrow SOIC-16 (3.9 mm body) lands only about 0.5 mm of each lead on the pad, which solders poorly. The 5.3 mm wide SOP package fits.
issues.evidence: U1-U7 footprint Package_SO:SOIC-16_4.55x10.3mm_P1.27mm, pads at ±3.25 mm, 1.6 mm long. U8 and U9 use the standard narrow SOIC-14 footprint.
issues.fix: Check which package was bought. For the next revision use SOIC-16_3.9x9.9mm if the parts are the narrow type.

issues.title: Output is not glitch-free when the selection changes
issues.detail: The output follows the selected input directly with no re-timing. Stepping Input0 or pulling reset low while the old or new clock is high can cut a pulse short or create a runt pulse on all 16 outputs. This remains after the cascade fix.
issues.evidence: U1-U4 Z outputs go to U9 (OR) and then U10/U11 buffers with no register in the path.
issues.fix: Step and reset only while the clocks involved are low. Check that the supertime sequences do this.

issues.title: Supply current of about 200 mA is abnormal
issues.detail: Eleven 74HC chips should draw well under 10 mA plus load current. Most of the excess is probably the damaged U6, but outputs driving a short would give a similar figure.
issues.evidence: Bench reading on 2026-11-18; U6 hot to the touch.
issues.fix: After replacing U5 and U6, recheck the current with J4 unplugged. If it is still high, check J4 orientation and look for another warm chip.

issues.title: No power-on reset
issues.detail: The counter starts at an arbitrary count until J2 is pulsed low, so the selected clock is undefined after power-up.
issues.evidence: ~MR net has no RC or supervisor; ~PE tied high with data inputs grounded.
issues.fix: Have supertime pulse reset after the board powers up, before the first sequence.

issues.title: Clock and data inputs float when undriven
issues.detail: Input0 to Input31 have no pull-down resistors. With the J1 cable unplugged or a channel undriven, Input0 can step the counter on noise and the other inputs draw extra supply current.
issues.evidence: Nets /Input0 to /Input31 each connect only J1 and one IC input.
issues.fix: Add 10 kΩ to 47 kΩ pull-down networks on J1 in the next revision.

issues.title: J4 uses a mirrored pin-socket footprint
issues.detail: If a header and ribbon cable are fitted instead of a socket, one orientation puts every output onto a ground wire and shorts all 16 buffers to ground through R1-R16. Because all outputs are identical, the other orientation works.
issues.evidence: J4 footprint Connector_PinSocket_2.54mm:PinSocket_2x16; pad 2 is at x = -2.54 mm from pad 1 (mirrored relative to a header).
issues.fix: Confirm that signals arrive on the odd wires at the far end before powering.

issues.title: 74HC inputs need 3.5 V for a high
issues.detail: NI card outputs meet this when lightly loaded, but a 3.3 V or weak TTL clock source would not switch the inputs reliably.
issues.evidence: All logic is 74HC on a 5 V rail.
issues.fix: If any source is 3.3 V or TTL-level, fit 74HCT parts, which are drop-in.

issues.title: Keep output edges at about 100 ns or faster
issues.detail: NI gives no maximum edge time for the clock inputs. The 6713 and 6733 have no stated hysteresis, so a slow, noisy edge could double-trigger; the 6534 has 500 mV of hysteresis. With 50 Ω series resistors, 470 pF gives roughly a 95 ns edge.
issues.evidence: NI 6711/6713, 6731/6733 and 6533/6534 specifications and manuals, read by a research subagent.
issues.fix: If C13-C28 are fitted, use 470 pF or less on all 16 outputs and confirm on a scope that no card double-updates.

issues.title: CLK0/1/2 net names are reversed
issues.detail: CLK0 goes to select line S2 and CLK2 to S0. The connections are correct, only the names are misleading.
issues.evidence: /CLK0 = U5.12 (Q2) to S2 pins; /CLK2 = U5.14 (Q0) to S0 pins.
issues.fix: Rename the nets in the next revision.

name: Supertime External Trigger (clock gate)
status_note: Gerbers were made in April 2024 and the PCB is fully routed (0 unconnected pads); the LTspice 'Gate to Trigger.asc' (op-amp comparator idea) is an older, unused approach superseded by the 74HCT123 monostable on this board.
description: A small 5 V digital board (38 x 50 mm, three SOIC chips, eight 2-pin Molex KK connectors) that lets the supertime 1 MHz update clock run only when the experiment allows it. The 1 MHz clock is ANDed with two gates. Gate 1 is (Supertime Resync OR a 60 Hz pulse); gate 2 is (Supertime Sorting OR FPGA input). To resync, supertime drives Resync low, which stops the clock; when the next 60 Hz trigger arrives, a CD74HCT123 monostable (R1 5k with C1 20nF, intended about 50 µs) makes a short pulse that lets the clock through again, so supertime restarts just after the 60 Hz edge. To hand control to the FPGA, supertime drives Sorting low, and the clock is released when the FPGA input goes high. Outputs are the gated '1 MHz Output' and the shaped '60 Hz Output' (for the FPGA). U1 = CD74HCT123 dual monostable (only half used), U2 = CD74HCT32 quad OR, U3 = CD74HCT08 quad AND. All inputs and outputs are bare connector pins straight onto the logic chips, with 100 nF + 1 µF decoupling per chip.

issues.title: Gate inputs float when nothing drives them
issues.detail: The Supertime Resync, Supertime Sorting, FPGA input and 60 Hz Trigger connectors go straight to CMOS-type inputs (HCT) with no pull-up or pull-down. When the NI card or FPGA is off, not yet configured, or the cable is unplugged, these inputs float, so the 1 MHz clock can stop, run, or chatter at random, and a floating 60 Hz Trigger can retrigger the monostable from noise. This is the same class of fault as the floating reset on the Multiplexer board.
issues.evidence: Nets /Supertime Resync (STRS1.1 -> U2.5 only), /Supertime Sorting (STSORT1.1 -> U2.2 only), /FPGA input (FPGA1.1 -> U2.1 only), /60 Hz Trigger (60HzIN1.1 -> U1.10 only). No resistor in the netlist except R1 (monostable timing). Per the schematic note, Resync and Sorting must idle high to let the clock run, FPGA input idle low.
issues.fix: Add 10k pull-ups to +5V on Resync and Sorting (idle = run), and 10k pull-downs on FPGA input and 60 Hz Trigger. Choose the defaults so that a disconnected board either runs or holds the clock in a known state.

issues.title: Unprotected inputs can be driven while board is unpowered
issues.detail: Every input pin goes directly to a 74HCT gate input whose internal clamp diode to +5V conducts if the pin is driven above the board supply. If an NI PCI-6534 line or the FPGA is driving a signal while this board's 5 V is off, current flows through the clamp diodes into the +5V rail, partly powering the chips through the decoupling caps and exceeding the roughly 20 mA clamp rating. The Multiplexer board lost a 74HC161 to this exact mechanism.
issues.evidence: U2.1, U2.2, U2.5 and U1.10 connect to the connectors with no series element; +5V net carries CP1-CP6 (total about 4.5 µF) and no bleed or protection on Vcc1. 74HCT inputs: abs max Vin = Vcc + 0.5 V, clamp current about 20 mA (standard HC/HCT data; not looked up online).
issues.fix: Put a 470 Ω to 1k series resistor in each input line, ideally with a pull resistor after it, and power this board before (or from the same supply sequencing as) the NI cards. Optionally add a small series Schottky or a clamp-diode-tolerant buffer.

issues.title: Combinational clock gating can create runt clock pulses
issues.detail: The output clock is a plain AND of the free-running 1 MHz clock with gate signals that change asynchronously to it (60 Hz monostable pulse, Resync, Sorting, FPGA). When a gate opens or closes while the clock is high, the output gets a truncated pulse of arbitrary width, which a counter may count or miss. That adds a one-tick uncertainty to exactly the resync/sort events this board exists to make deterministic. The 60 Hz monostable edge is asynchronous to the 1 MHz clock by construction, so this happens every 60 Hz cycle during a resync.
issues.evidence: /1 MHz Output = U3.6 = U3.4 AND U3.5; U3.4 = U3.3 = (U3.1 AND 1 MHz Clock U3.2); U3.1 = U2.6 = OR of Resync and /60 Hz Output (U1.5). The designer's LTspice file models the gating with ideal gates and cannot show this ('Monostable multivibrator cannot be simulated').
issues.fix: Synchronise the enable: latch the combined gate with a D flip-flop or transparent latch (e.g. 74HC74 or 74HC573) clocked on the falling edge of the 1 MHz clock before the final AND, so the gate only changes while the clock is low.

issues.title: Outputs are unbuffered with no series resistor
issues.detail: The 1 MHz Output (U3.6) and 60 Hz Output (U1.5) drive the connectors and cables directly from HCT gate outputs. A short, cable fault, or connection to a powered-off NI/FPGA input will load a gate output beyond its rating or backfeed it, and a long unterminated cable gives ringing on the clock that can double-count edges. The only mitigation is an optional 100 pF cap, which stores charge and can worsen ringing rather than damp it.
issues.evidence: Nets /1 MHz Output: U3.6, 1MHzOut1.1, C2.1; /60 Hz Output: U1.5, U2.4, 60HzOut1.1 with no resistor. Silkscreen: 'Option output cap to reduce overshoot (C2~100pF)', 'Output to high impedance'. Schematic note says C2 'may or may not be included in the actual circuit, one should check'.
issues.fix: Add a 33-50 Ω series resistor at each output connector (and consider a 74HCT244-type buffer for the 60 Hz output so the monostable is not loaded by the cable). Decide on C2 and record whether it is fitted.

issues.title: 5 V HCT outputs may overdrive 3.3 V FPGA/NI inputs
issues.detail: The 60 Hz Output goes to an FPGA, and HCT logic swings to about 4.5-5 V. If that FPGA input is 3.3 V LVCMOS and not 5 V tolerant, it will be overstressed. The FPGA input (return signal) is fine in the other direction since HCT accepts 2 V as high.
issues.evidence: U1 CD74HCT123, U2, U3 all on +5V net; 60HzOut1 labelled 'Outputs: 60Hz Trig to FPGA' in silkscreen.
issues.fix: Confirm the FPGA I/O standard; if 3.3 V, use a series resistor plus clamp or a level shifter (74LVC) on that output.

issues.title: Pulse width of the monostable is not clearly 50 µs
issues.detail: The note states 5k and 20nF give about 50 µs, but R times C is 100 µs and the actual width depends on the datasheet constant and on capacitor tolerance and voltage coefficient. A 1206 ceramic (if X7R/Y5V) at 20 nF can shift by 10-20 percent. Also 5k is near the minimum recommended timing resistor for 5 V operation. The LTspice file used a 1 µs pulse, so the simulation does not reflect the built value.
issues.evidence: R1 = 5kΩ (+5V to U1.7), C1 = 20nF (U1.6 to U1.7), U1.9 (2A) GND, U1.10 (2B) = 60 Hz trigger, U1.11 (2R) +5V. Timing constant not checked against the CD74HCT123 datasheet.
issues.fix: Measure the real pulse width on 60 Hz Output with a scope and record it on the schematic; use a C0G capacitor for C1 if width matters.

issues.title: No reverse-polarity or bulk protection on 5 V input
issues.detail: Vcc1 is a 2-pin Molex header with no diode or fuse; reversed wiring would apply 5 V backwards to all three ICs. The 10 µF bulk cap is stated to be 'off board'.
issues.evidence: Vcc1.1 on +5V, Vcc1.2 on GND, PWR_FLAGs only; schematic note '10µF tantalum cap for global decoupling on PS inputs (off board)'.
issues.fix: Add a series Schottky diode or P-FET and a local 10 µF cap, or label polarity clearly on silkscreen.

issues.title: Docs: schematic/PCB naming differences only; part names say E but SOIC fitted
issues.detail: DRC reports 14 net_conflict warnings and 20 footprint library overrides, but all net conflicts are only net-name differences (Net-(C1-Pad1) vs Net-(U1-2CX), unconnected pad names), not real connectivity differences; no unconnected pads. ERC has 137 warnings (95 off-grid endpoints, library mismatches, missing library CD74HCT123E/32E/08E symbols), none electrical. Symbols are named for DIP (E) while values and footprints are SOIC (M96); package pinouts and SOIC-16/SOIC-14 footprints match the parts, unlike the sister board.
issues.evidence: DRC: 0 unconnected pads, 14 net_conflict (names only), 20 lib_footprint_mismatch. ERC: 137 warnings. U1 SOIC-16 pin1..16 pads and U2/U3 SOIC-14 match 74HCT123/32/08 pinouts.
issues.fix: Update library symbols when convenient; no board change needed for this item. Add connector pin labels (signal/GND) to silkscreen.

optional output smoothing cap on 1 MHz Output; schematic says it may not be fitted
unknown_parts.suggested: State DNP or fitted; prefer a 33-50 Ω series resistor instead

name: Digital Buffer IC Evaluation Board V2 (8-channel 74HC/HCT244)
folder: Digital Buffer IC evaluation board V2
files: Digital Buffer IC evaluation board V2.kicad_sch
Digital Buffer IC evaluation board V2.kicad_pcb
Digital Buffer IC evaluation board V2.csv
status_note: Complete schematic and routed 50.8 x 63.5 mm board with no unrouted nets; I cannot tell from the files whether it was ever assembled. Supersedes V1.
description: An 8-channel digital buffer board built around one octal buffer/line driver in an SOIC-20W (silkscreen says SN74HCT244DWR, schematic says 74HC244) powered from a 2-pin +5 V connector with 100 nF and 1 µF decoupling. Each channel has a 2-pin KK-254 input connector (signal pin 1, ground pin 2) feeding a 50 Ω series resistor, then a node with a 5 kΩ pull-up to +5 V and a 1 nF capacitor to ground, then the buffer input. Each buffer output drives a 1 nF capacitor to ground and a 50 Ω series resistor into the output connector. Both output-enable pins are tied to ground so all outputs are always on. An unconnected input reads high, so the output reads high. It was designed to test whether this kind of buffer can clean up and fan out timing signals from the NI digital pattern card, with the RC filters on input and output as optional edge-smoothing.

issues.title: Part is HC in schematic but HCT on the silkscreen
issues.detail: The schematic symbol/value is 74HC244 while the board silkscreen says SN74HCT244DWR. A plain HC part at 5 V needs about 3.5 V for a high input, which many TTL-level sources (2.4 V minimum high) and 3.3 V logic do not guarantee; the 5 kΩ pull-up only partly rescues this. HCT accepts 2.0 V as high. Using the wrong one gives marginal or missed edges that look like intermittent failures.
issues.evidence: U1 value '74HC244' in nets.txt and schematic; B.SilkS/F.SilkS text 'SN74HCT244DWR'. Supply +5V on U1.20.
issues.fix: Fit the 74HCT244 (or ideally also test an LVC/AHCT244) and change the schematic value and symbol to match. Do not populate a 74HC244 if the source is TTL-level.

issues.title: Input and output 1 nF filter capacitors slow the edges being evaluated
issues.detail: Input: 50 Ω plus source impedance with 1 nF gives roughly 50-100 ns time constant, so edges slow to about 100-200 ns before reaching the buffer. Output: the 1 nF sits on the IC side of the 50 Ω, so the 244 drives 1 nF directly and its edges are also slowed (and the capacitor does nothing to damp cable ringing at the far end). The schematic note says the output capacitor space will likely remain unused, yet all 16 are shown as 1 nF with no DNP mark and the silkscreen says 'LP filter may or may not be necessary'. A built board can differ from what the schematic implies.
issues.evidence: C1-C8 (1nF) from Net-(U1-1A0..2A3) to GND with R1-R8 50 Ω in series from INn; C9-C16 (1nF) from Net-(U1-1Y0..2Y3) to GND, then R17-R24 50 Ω to OUTn. Schematic note: 'I'm putting space for a capacitor on the output ... likely remain unused'.
issues.fix: Mark which of C1-C16 are populated (DNP the rest) and record this in the schematic and on the board. For timing-edge evaluation start with C1-C16 unfitted, then add input capacitors only if needed. The 50 Ω series is the proper source termination for a 50 Ω cable only if the 244 output impedance is small; measure on the actual cable.

issues.title: Weak input protection and back-powering path through pull-ups
issues.detail: The only protection is the 50 Ω series resistor plus the IC's internal clamp diodes. An overvoltage (for example 12 V) would drive well over the 20 mA clamp rating. If a high signal is applied while the board is unpowered, current flows through the input clamp and the 5 kΩ pull-up into the +5V rail and can partially power the board. Low risk for NI 5 V digital signals.
issues.evidence: IN1.1 -> R1 (50 Ω) -> U1.2; R9 5 kΩ from +5V to the same node; no diodes or clamps in the netlist. PWRV1 +5V connector has no reverse-polarity or overvoltage protection.
issues.fix: If the board will see other equipment, raise the series resistor to about 100-330 Ω in front of the pull-up node or add a Schottky clamp pair; add a series diode or polarised connector keying note on the +5V input.

issues.title: Decoupling capacitors are far from the IC supply pin
issues.detail: CP1 (100 nF) and CP2 (1 µF) sit near the power connector at the top of the board, roughly 8-11 mm of trace from U1 VCC (pin 20). With eight outputs driving 1 nF loads, switching currents at the IC are larger than for a normal buffer and the local rail may bounce. A 100 nF should be next to pins 20/10.
issues.evidence: CP1 at (146.05, 69.85), CP2 at (151.13, 69.85) mm; U1 pin 20 at about (153.2, 75.6) mm; pads 10 and 19 are GND. DRC also reports one starved thermal on GND pad 19 of U1 (1 spoke, 2 required).
issues.fix: On a respin, put a 100 nF immediately across U1.20 to U1.10 with a short ground path. This is low priority unless supply noise or ringing is observed.

issues.title: Stale BOM CSV in the project folder does not match the design
issues.detail: The exported csv lists 18 capacitors (C1 100 nF, C2 1 µF) and assigns 5 kΩ to R1, R4, R7 etc. and 50 Ω to R2, R3 etc. That is a different reference numbering from the current schematic (CP1/CP2 decoupling, R1-R8 and R17-R24 = 50 Ω, R9-R16 = 5 kΩ). Ordering parts from the csv would produce a wrong, unworkable board.
issues.evidence: csv: 'C3...C18 1nF', 'R1, R4, R7, R10, R13, R16, R19, R22 = 5kΩ', generated with Eeschema 6.0.1 on 2024-04-12, component count 62; nets.txt/schematic: 16 x 1 nF + CP1 100 nF + CP2 1 µF, 24 resistors.
issues.fix: Regenerate the BOM from the current schematic before ordering and delete or archive the old csv.

issues.detail: Pinout was checked against the 74x244: 1A0-1A3 on pins 2/4/6/8 map to 1Y0-1Y3 on 18/16/14/12, 2A0-2A3 on 17/15/13/11 map to 2Y0-2Y3 on 3/5/7/9, OE pins 1 and 19 are on GND, VCC pin 20, GND pin 10. issues.title: Evaluated alternatives (LS07, LVC1G17, F244) are not on this board
issues.detail: The LTspice files cover LS07 (open collector, needs pull-up, 120 pF load, R stepped 100 Ω-1 kΩ), SN74LVC1G17 and SN74F244N (with 50/5k input network and 50 Ω output, load 10 pF/15 nH/1 MΩ). If an LVC244 is tried on this footprint, it must be supplied from 3.3 V or less (LVC family max 5.5 V but outputs only reach VCC), and the +5V pull-ups and silkscreen would need to change. The F244 is a 5 V TTL part with different input thresholds.

name: Digital Buffer IC Evaluation Board V1 (6-channel SN74LS07)
folder: Digital Buffer IC evaluation board V1
status_note: First 6-channel open-collector SN74LS07 test board (silkscreen 02/2024); replaced by the 8-channel 74HC244 board V2 which adds input pull-ups and output series resistors.
description: A small 42.7 x 35.6 mm board that copies six logic inputs to six outputs through one SN74LS07 hex open-collector buffer (SOIC-14) powered from a 2-pin +5 V connector with 100 nF and 1 µF decoupling. Each channel has a 2-pin Molex KK-254 input and output connector (signal on pin 1, ground on pin 2). Each input has an optional 0 Ω jumper (W1-W6) to ground so an unused input can be tied low. The outputs are open-collector and the board has no pull-up resistors, so a pull-up to +5 V (or other rail up to 30 V) must be supplied by the receiving end for the output to ever go high. It was made to test whether a buffer could clean up and fan out timing signals from the NI digital card.

issues.title: Open-collector outputs have no pull-up resistors on board
issues.detail: The SN74LS07 can only pull its outputs low. With nothing on the output connector, or with a receiver that has no pull-up, the output never goes high and a scope or digital input will see a stuck low or floating line. This is the likely reason V2 was built with a push-pull 244.
issues.evidence: Nets Net-(OUT1-Pin_1)..Net-(OUT6-Pin_1) each contain only U1 output pin (2,4,6,8,10,12; type open_collector) and the OUTn.1 connector pin; no resistor to +5V anywhere in the netlist.
issues.fix: Do not use V1 as a drop-in buffer. If kept, add pull-up pads (about 330 Ω to 1 kΩ for cable loads) to +5V on each output, or pull up at the receiver. Use V2 (HC/HCT244) for true push-pull driving.

issues.title: Unused inputs float unless a 0 Ω jumper is fitted; jumpers short sources
issues.detail: Unused LS inputs left open float and can pick up noise, but fitting W1-W6 hard-shorts the input connector pin 1 to ground. If a jumper is fitted on a channel and a signal source is then connected, the source is shorted to ground with no series resistance.
issues.evidence: W1-W3 pin 1 on GND, pin 2 on Net-(IN1..3-Pin_1); W4-W6 pin 2 on GND, pin 1 on Net-(IN4..6-Pin_1). All 0 Ω, 1206. Silkscreen says unused inputs must have pull-down W1-W6, 1000-5000 ohm will work.

name: AND gate with bypass for RF trigger
status_note: Complete, titled single-sheet schematic (rev 000) with no board; likely a small box built on perfboard.
description: A one-gate logic box that gates a microwave trigger with an RF-trigger signal. Four BNC-style coax connectors: RF Coax and Microwave Coax are inputs, Output Coax is the result, and Power Coax supplies 5 V and ground. A 74HCT08 AND gate combines them: pin 1A is fed from a switch that selects either the RF Coax signal or a fixed +5V (bypass), pin 1B takes the Microwave Coax signal, and 1Y goes to the Output Coax. With the switch in the bypass position the output simply follows the microwave signal. The IC has a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor.

issues.title: Inputs float when a cable is unplugged and have no termination
issues.detail: The gate inputs connect directly to coax centres with no pull-down or termination. With the RF cable removed (switch in RF position) or the microwave cable removed, the CMOS input floats and the output may oscillate or sit in a random state. A 50 Ω pulse source driving this high-impedance input also reflects and can overshoot.
issues.evidence: U.1 (1A) via SW.2/SW.1 from J RF Coax; U.2 (1B) from J Microwave Coax; no resistors in the schematic
issues.fix: Add 10-100 kΩ pull-downs on pins 1 and 2 and a 50 Ω termination (or series resistor) per input as the source requires.

issues.title: 5 V power on a coax connector the same as the signal connectors
issues.detail: The power input is a coax of the same type as the three signal connectors. Plugging a signal cable into the power jack, or the power cable into a signal jack, would put 5 V onto test equipment or overdrive the gate. There is no reverse-polarity or over-voltage protection on the supply.
issues.evidence: Power Coax (5V/GND): J.1 to +5V, J.2 to GND; same Conn_Coaxial symbol as the other three
issues.fix: Use a distinct connector type for power (barrel or different gender) and add a series diode or fuse; label the box.

issues.title: No input clamp, and output has no series resistor
issues.detail: Pulse sources above 5.5 V or ringing could exceed the HCT input absolute maximum (VCC+0.5 V). The output drives coax directly with a CMOS gate.
issues.evidence: U.1, U.2 straight from connectors; U.3 straight to Output Coax
issues.fix: Add 100-470 Ω series resistors and optionally Schottky clamps at the inputs; 50 Ω in series at the output.

issues.title: Switch wiring and pinout verified; ERC is noise
issues.detail: The SPDT switch common (pin 2) goes to 1A with throws to RF Coax (pin 1) and +5V (pin 3), as intended. 74HCT08 pinout matches; unused gates have inputs at GND and outputs open. ERC: 46 off-grid endpoints, library mismatches, 4 dangling wires, no effect on circuit. HCT thresholds (VIH about 2 V) suit TTL-level triggers; a 3.3 V logic source also works.
issues.fix: None needed.

name: Strobe generator and DDS timing control
folder: Strobe generator and DDS Timing Control
files: Strobe generator and DDS Timing Control.kicad_sch
status_note: Schematic only, all references are unannotated (U?, R?, C?) and R/C values are blank, so pulse widths are undefined; no board exists.
description: A small 5 V logic card that takes a clock and two enable signals from the supertime system and produces two outputs for the DDS. CLK OUT is the input clock passed through an AND gate that is enabled when SUPERTIME or PCIE is high (74HCT32 OR into 74HCT08 AND). PULSE OUT comes from a chain of three one-shot timers (CD74HCT123, two per chip): the clock edges each start a timed delay, and the end of that delay starts a second one-shot that makes the output pulse, presumably the strobe or I/O-update pulse for the DDS. The input header J1 carries 5V, GND, CLK, SUPERTIME and PCIE; output header J2 carries CLK OUT and PULSE OUT. The delay and pulse widths are set by three RC pairs whose values are not filled in.

issues.title: KiCad sees only the +5V net; wires do not connect to pins
issues.detail: The KiCad-generated netlist contains only the +5V net, and the ERC reports 10 dangling wires and 8 GND power symbols with unconnected pins. Visually the sheet looks wired, but the GND symbols sit off the wire ends (e.g. at 153.924,110.363 versus the wire end at 153.67,109.22) and many wire ends do not land on pin ends in KiCad's eyes. As it stands the file cannot be used to make a board or a trustworthy netlist.
issues.evidence: nets.txt lists a single net (+5V); ERC: 10x wire_dangling, #PWR0101..0109 'Pin not connected'; all refs are U?/R?/C?/J? (duplicate designators)
issues.fix: Re-annotate the parts, move GND/+5V symbols onto wire ends, re-run ERC until the connectivity matches the drawing, and only then trust the netlist. The connectivity described below was traced by me from wire and pin geometry, not from KiCad's netlist.

issues.title: Pulse widths and delays are undefined (R and C blank)
issues.detail: All three one-shots need an external resistor and capacitor and the timing is the whole purpose of the card, but R1-R3 and C1-C3 are plain 'R' and 'C'. Nobody can tell what delay or strobe width is intended, and the CD74HCT123 has limits on the allowed Rext/Cext range (check the TI datasheet: roughly t = 0.7 to 1 x R x C, and a minimum Rext of a few kΩ at 5 V).
issues.evidence: R2/C1 on U1 pins 7/6, R3/C3 on U1 pins 15/14, R1/C2 on U3 pins 15/14; all with value 'R' or 'C'
issues.fix: Write down the required delay after the clock edge and the pulse width needed by the DDS, choose Rext/Cext (low-leakage film or C0G, not X7R, for stable timing), and add a trimmer in one leg if the timing needs tuning.

issues.title: Each clock period appears to produce two pulses on PULSE OUT
issues.detail: U1 monostable 1 triggers on the falling CLK edge (pin 1 *1A, pin 2 1B at +5V) and its 1Q output (pin 13) drives U3 pin 1 (*1A); the end of that pulse falls and triggers U3. U1 monostable 2 triggers on the rising CLK edge (pin 10 2B, pin 9 *2A at GND) and its *2Q output (pin 12) drives U3 pin 2 (1B), whose rising edge at the end of that pulse triggers U3 a second time. So U3 1Q (PULSE OUT) fires once after each falling edge and once after each rising edge, with two different delays (R3C3 and R2C1). If a single delayed strobe per clock was intended, this is not what is drawn.
issues.fix: Confirm the intended behaviour with a timing diagram. If only one delayed pulse per clock is wanted, remove one of the two U1 monostables from the chain (e.g. tie U3 pin 2 high and use only the *1A path).

issues.title: No decoupling capacitors on any of the four logic ICs
issues.detail: Four HCT chips, two of them containing one-shots driving analog-sensitive RC timing nodes, have no bypass capacitor. Supply bounce from output edges will shift or retrigger the one-shot pulses.
issues.evidence: VCC pins U1.16, U3.16, U2.14, U4.14 on +5V; the only C parts are the three timing capacitors
issues.fix: Add 100 nF ceramic at each VCC pin and a 10 µF bulk capacitor at J1 pin 1.

issues.title: Output header J2 has no ground pin
issues.detail: CLK OUT and PULSE OUT leave on a 2-pin header (pin 1 CLK OUT, pin 2 PULSE OUT) with no ground. The return path for the DDS board would be an unknown wire, giving ground bounce and ringing on these fast edges.
issues.evidence: J2.1 = U2.3 (CLK OUT), J2.2 = U3.13 (PULSE OUT); no GND on J2
issues.fix: Use a 4-pin header (or coax connectors) with ground between or beside each signal, and add a small series resistor (22-50 Ω) at each output.

issues.title: CLK OUT gate is asynchronous: enable changes can create runt clock pulses
issues.detail: CLK OUT = CLK AND (SUPERTIME OR PCIE). If either enable changes while CLK is high, a truncated clock pulse is passed to the output. PULSE OUT is not gated at all and runs from the raw CLK.
issues.evidence: U4.1 = J1.4 (SUPERTIME), U4.2 = J1.5 (PCIE), U4.3 -> U2.2, U2.1 = CLK, U2.3 = CLK OUT; U1.1/U1.10 take CLK directly
issues.fix: If the enables are not already synchronous to CLK, latch them with a flip-flop clocked on CLK's inactive edge. Confirm that an ungated PULSE OUT is intended.

issues.title: Output levels are 5 V HCT; DDS inputs may be 3.3 V
issues.detail: The HCT outputs swing to about 5 V. AD9852-class DDS parts use 3.3 V logic on their control inputs and may not be 5 V tolerant. Inputs from the supertime/NI 5 V TTL side are fine for HCT (VIH about 2 V).
issues.evidence: U2.3 and U3.13 are 74HCT outputs from a +5V supply to J2
issues.fix: Check the DDS board's input rating; if it is 3.3 V only, use a 74LVC buffer on 3.3 V or a resistor divider. I did not look up the AD9852 datasheet, so this is unverified.

issues.title: Unused inputs are tied correctly; pin numbers match the real parts
issues.detail: Unused gate inputs (U2 and U4 gates 2-4) and the unused second monostable of U3 (pins 9, 10, 11 to GND) are tied low and outputs left open, which is correct. Pin numbers match the 74HCT08/32 and CD74HCT123 pinouts. The CD74HCT123 outputs can glitch at power-up, so PULSE OUT may emit one stray pulse when 5 V is applied.
issues.fix: Nothing required; ignore the power-up pulse or hold the DDS update input inactive until after power-up.

name: JR65RC unknown board (LF356 amplifier)
status_note: Reverse-engineered one-stage sketch with blank R/C values and no power connector; empty board file.
description: This looks like a reverse-engineered sketch of a single-stage current-to-voltage (transimpedance) amplifier. A coax input feeds the inverting input of an LF356 JFET op amp, the non-inverting input is grounded to the coax shield, and a resistor in parallel with a capacitor sits from output to inverting input. The output goes to a second coax connector. The op amp runs from ±15 V with a bypass capacitor on each rail. Typical use would be amplifying a photodiode current, but the name 'JR65RC' and the source device are unknown, so this is an inference from the topology.

issues.title: Feedback R and C unknown; stability depends on them
issues.detail: The gain is set by R and the bandwidth and stability by the parallel C. With a coax cable (tens of pF) on the inverting input and no value for C, an LF356 transimpedance stage can ring or oscillate.

issues.title: Input and output coax have no protection or isolation

issues.evidence: J?.1 on U.2; U.6 on output J?.1 with no series part
issues.fix: Add about 50 Ω series at the output and, if the input is exposed, a small series resistor and clamp diodes.

issues.title: No power input drawn; NULL pins open; ERC noise

name: Lattice intensity lock (PI servo board, newest version)
status_note: Newest and most complete of the four copies: 4-layer board (Dec 2023) fully routed with no unrouted nets in DRC, but the schematic was edited in Sep 2025 after the board and BOM (five component values and U17 part changed) and J4 pin numbering differs between schematic and board.
description: This is the PI (proportional plus integral) controller that holds the optical lattice laser intensity constant. A photodiode signal enters J2 and goes through an AD8429 instrumentation amplifier (gain about 1). One of two setpoints, each set by an external pot fed from a 10 V MAX876 reference (J5 and J7, buffered by OP177s U2 and U5), is picked by an analog switch (U6, digital line Dig1). A difference amplifier (U7) forms error = setpoint minus photodiode, and the same switch (Dig2) either passes that error or forces it to 0 V; a follower (U13) buffers it. The error feeds a proportional stage (U9, gain set by trimmer RV1) and an integrator (IVC102 U10 with hold/clear controlled by Dig3 and Dig4, speed set by trimmer RV2); the two are summed by U11. The result can optionally go through a voltage-controlled-gain stage (VCA810, U14, driven from J3 through AMP03 U17, enabled by solder jumper W1), then through a zener clamp built from two op amps (U8, U15, D1/D2) to J11 'VControl', which drives the AOM/RF modulator driver. J6 gives monitor outputs of the integrator and the error. Supplies are +15 V/-15 V on J1, with local +5 V (LDK320 U12) and -5 V (LM79L05 U16) for the VCA810. Signal flow as wired: control = +(Kp + Ki/s) x (setpoint - photodiode), so the loop is negative feedback only if raising VControl raises the detected light (not determined by this board).

issues.title: R11 and R12 are either/or links but both are listed as fitted
issues.detail: R11 sends the unclamped signal straight to the output connector; R12 sends the clamped one. They are meant as a choice, but both are 0 Ω in the schematic and BOM with no do-not-fit mark. With both fitted the zener clamp is defeated and the AOM driver sees the unclamped voltage.
issues.fix: Check which is fitted on the working board. Fit only R12 (clamp in use) unless there is a reason to bypass it, and mark R11 as not fitted.

issues.title: Output clamp voltage is not defined (generic D_Zener, R14 = 0 ohm)
issues.detail: D1 and D2 are back-to-back generic zeners (anodes joined, D2 cathode to GND), giving a symmetric clamp of +/-(Vz + 0.7 V) that protects the RF modulator input, but no zener voltage is specified anywhere, so the protection level is unknown. R14 is now 0 ohm (it was 1k in the Dec 2023 BOM/board), so U8 drives the zeners with no current limit and sits in its output current limit whenever clamping, heating U8 and the zeners. The symmetric clamp also allows negative output of the same size, which an RF VCA/AOM driver with a 0 to +V control input may not tolerate.
issues.evidence: D1.1[K]/R14.1/U15.3 = Net-(D1-K); D1.2/D2.2 = Net-(D1-A); D2.1[K] = GND; D1, D2 value 'D_Zener'; R14 = 0k (board footprint value still 1k).
issues.fix: Choose Vz just under the AOM driver's maximum control voltage (and decide whether negative excursions need a separate Schottky clamp to GND), specify the part (SOD-123 500 mW), and restore a series resistor in R14 (about 330 ohm to 1k) so the zener current is limited.

issues.title: VCA810 input is driven well beyond its +/-5 V rating
issues.detail: U14 (VCA810) runs from +5 V/-5 V, and its input voltage limit is the supply (+/-VS, abs max supply +/-6.5 V, from TI datasheet search). Its + input is connected directly to the output of U11, which runs on +/-15 V and swings to about +/-13 V whenever the integrator or P term is large, for example at start-up, when the lock is open or when the error gate is switched on. There is no series resistor, attenuator or clamp at U14 pin 1, so ESD diodes conduct and the part can be damaged or latch up. The gain-control pin is also driven straight from U17 (+/-13 V capable) while the VCA810 expects 0 to -2 V.
issues.evidence: Net-(U14-+In): R10.1, U11.6 (output), U14.1[+In], W1.1. +5V: U14.6, -5V: U14.7. /GC: U14.3, U17.5, U17.6. No component between U11.6 and U14.1.
issues.fix: Add an input divider/series resistor with clamp diodes to the 5 V rails at U14.1 (or limit U11 to about +/-3 V), and limit or divide the GC drive so it stays inside the VCA810 control range. Confirm absolute maximum values in the TI VCA810 datasheet.

issues.title: Digital control inputs have no pull resistors and may not see a valid high
issues.detail: Dig1 and Dig2 go straight to the CMOS analog switch inputs (U6 IN1 and IN2) and Dig3/Dig4 to the IVC102 switch pins with only connector J4 attached, so with the cable unplugged or the NI card not yet driving, the setpoint select, error gate and integrator hold/clear state are undefined at power-up. Also the DG303A data sheet gives logic 1 as 4.0 V minimum (logic 0 at most 0.8 V), which a 3.3 V or marginal 5 V TTL output from the digital I/O card may not reach, so Dig1/Dig2 high may be unreliable. Per the DG303A truth table, IN2 high = error passed, IN2 low = error forced to 0 V.
issues.evidence: /Dig1: J4.1, U6.6 (IN1); /Dig2: J4.3, U6.11 (IN2); /Dig3: J4.5, U10.11 (S1); /Dig4: J4.7, U10.12 (S2). No R or driver on these nets. U6 V+ = +15 V, V- = -15 V, GND pin 7.
issues.fix: Add pull-down resistors (about 10k) to the safe state on all four lines (Dig2 low = error zero is the safe default) and put a 5 V buffer (74HC/74AHCT type) on Dig1 and Dig2 so the 4 V level is met; check the IVC102 S1/S2 polarity and thresholds against its datasheet.

issues.title: J4 pin numbers differ between schematic and board
issues.detail: In the schematic Dig1..Dig4 are on J4 pins 1, 3, 5, 7 and GND on the even pins. On the board (and its silkscreen, which reads Dig 1, GND, Dig 2, GND... from the left) GND is on pins 1, 3, 5, 7 and Dig4, Dig3, Dig2, Dig1 are on pins 2, 4, 6, 8. A cable made from the schematic will connect Dig1 to ground and send Dig signals to the wrong functions; DRC reports 8 net_conflict items for exactly these pads. This looks like a leftover from a schematic edit that was not pushed to the PCB.
issues.evidence: pcb.txt J4: 1:GND 2:/Dig4 3:GND 4:/Dig3 5:GND 6:/Dig2 7:GND 8:/Dig1. nets.txt: /Dig1 J4.1, /Dig2 J4.3, /Dig3 J4.5, /Dig4 J4.7, GND J4.2/4/6/8. Same mismatch present in the ver2 board.
issues.fix: Decide which numbering is authoritative (the board is what exists), update the schematic to match it, and document the J4 pinout (including which end is pin 1) on silkscreen and in the lab notes.

issues.title: Schematic values changed after layout; board/BOM disagree with schematic
issues.detail: The Sep 2025 schematic differs from the Dec 2023 board and BOM in five places: C17 100pF vs 100nF, R14 0 vs 1k, R15 2k vs 3M, R16 560 vs 20k, U17 AMP03 vs INA105KU. C17 sets the integrator capacitance, so 100 nF versus 100 pF is a factor 1000 in integrator speed; R15/R16 set how much the error is attenuated. It is unclear which values are on the boards that were built and tested.
issues.evidence: ERC/DRC footprint_symbol_mismatch: C17, R14, R15 (3M), R16 (20k), U17 (INA105KU); csv Dec 2023: C17 100nF, R14 1k, R15 3M, R16 20k, U17 INA105KU; ver4.net identical topology with old values; nets.txt now C17 100pF, R14 0k, R15 2k, R16 560, U17 AMP03.
issues.fix: Record which values are fitted on the working board, update the BOM and PCB footprint values from the schematic (or revert), and note that INA105 and AMP03 are different parts with different internal resistors/pin functions on pin 1 and 8.

issues.title: Error gate divider attenuates the error to about 78 percent
issues.detail: The error gate uses series R16 and a shunt switch path: with Dig2 high, the error node is loaded by R15 to ground and U7 sees R16+R15 as load; with Dig2 low, the node is shorted to ground and U7 drives R16 (560 ohm) into ground. With R16 = 560 and R15 = 2k the passed error is R15/(R15+R16) = 0.78 plus switch on-resistance, so every gain setting is 22 percent lower than the 2023 values (20k/3M, 0.993) gave. In the zero state U7 delivers up to about 24 mA at +/-13.5 V into 560 ohm.
issues.evidence: /Err/Gnd: R16.1, U6.13[D2], U6.14[D4], U13.3. U6.12[S2] via R15.2 (2k) to GND; U6.15[S4] on GND. R16 between U7.6 and the node.
issues.fix: Return to R16 about 20k and R15 about 1M or more unless the attenuation was intended, or buffer U7 differently, and keep U7 load below 5 mA.

issues.title: Trimmers RV1 and RV2 used as rheostats with the third pin floating
issues.detail: RV1 (P gain) uses pin 1 and wiper pin 2 with pin 3 unconnected, and RV2 (I gain) uses pin 3 and wiper pin 2 with pin 1 unconnected. If the wiper of RV1 loses contact (vibration, dirty carbon track) the feedback path of U9 opens and U9 saturates to a rail, which then goes into U11 and the VCA/clamp and J11. Min P gain is 0 as R6 is 0 ohm.
issues.evidence: Net-(R6-Pad1): R6.1, RV1.1; Net-(R7-Pad2): R7.2, RV1.2, U9.6; unconnected-(RV1-Pad3); Net-(R9-Pad1): R9.1, RV2.3; Net-(U10-IIN): RV2.2, U10.2; unconnected-(RV2-Pad1).
issues.fix: Tie the unused end of each trimmer to its wiper, and put a fixed resistor in series with the minimum so the P gain cannot be exactly 0 or the feedback open.

issues.title: No automatic anti-windup; integrator only controlled by manual hold/clear
issues.detail: The integrator output is limited only by the IVC102 and U11 rails, while the zener clamp is after the summing amplifier. When the output sits at the clamp (for example during the lock-to-unlock transition) the integrator keeps ramping, and when the error changes sign it must unwind before the output leaves the clamp. The IVC102 hold and clear pins (Dig3/Dig4) allow the supertime program to freeze or reset it, and Dig2 zeroes the error, but nothing is automatic, and Dig3/Dig4 have no defined default (see digital input issue).
issues.evidence: U10 pins 11 (S1) and 12 (S2) on /Dig3 and /Dig4; clamp D1/D2 after U8; U11 sums R7 (P) and R8 (I) with R10 = 1k feedback.
issues.fix: Procedurally reset the integrator (Dig3/Dig4 clear) before each acquisition, or add a back-calculation/limiter around U11 or U10 (diode clamp on the integrator output).

issues.title: Monitor outputs J6 are unbuffered, no ground pin, no series resistance
issues.detail: J6 pin 1 is wired directly to the IVC102 output node (/V_int, which also feeds R8 and C17), so a cable or scope probe adds capacitance to the integrator output and a short on the connector pins disturbs the lock. Pin 2 is the U4 LF356 follower output, directly on the connector. The connector has only these two pins, so there is no ground reference.
issues.fix: Buffer /V_int with a follower plus 100-1k series resistor like the error output, and add a GND pin to J6.

issues.title: Unplugged setpoint pots or open W1 leave inputs floating
issues.detail: J5 and J7 carry the 10 V reference, the wiper and ground for the external setpoint pots. With a pot unplugged the OP177 follower input (U2.3/U5.3) floats and drifts to a rail, so the error goes to the rail when that setpoint is selected. Similarly W1 is drawn as 'Jumper_3_Open' (no bridge), leaving the clamp/VCA chain input U8.3 not tied to the controller.
issues.evidence: Net-(J5-Pin_2): J5.2, U2.3; Net-(J7-Pin_2): J7.2, U5.3; Net-(J5-Pin_1): J5.1, J7.1, U3.6; W1 'Jumper_3_Open' with pad 2 on Net-(U8-+).
issues.fix: Add a high-value resistor from each wiper to ground (or a default fixed divider) and document W1: solder A-C (no VCA810) or B-C (VCA810 in path) before use.

issues.title: PI corner frequency cannot be determined; trimmer values missing
issues.detail: Proportional gain is Kp = (R6 + RV1)/R5 with R5 = 1k and R6 = 0 ohm. The integrator gain is Ki = 1/((R9 + RV2) x Cint) where Cint = the IVC102 internal 100 pF (C1, C2, C3 pins all tied to the summing node, assumed 10+30+60 pF) plus C17 = 100 pF, so about 200 pF, and R9 = 0 ohm. The PI corner is fc = Ki/(2 pi Kp). Example only: RV1 = RV2 = 10k gives Kp = 10, Ki = 5e5 per second and fc about 8 kHz. RV1 and RV2 values are not given in the schematic ('R_PP', 'R_PI'), so the actual corner is unknown; the sheet note also says 100 pF internal where the earlier Copy sheet says 1000 pF.
issues.evidence: RV1 = R_PP, RV2 = R_PI (R_Potentiometer_Trim_US, Bourns 3214X); R5 1k; R6 0k; R9 0k; C17 100pF; U10 pins 4,5,6 on Net-(U10-C1) with C17.2 and U10.3.
issues.fix: Set RV1 and RV2 values (for example 10k or 100k) in the schematic and calculate the corner range; check the IVC102 datasheet for the internal capacitance on pins 4-6.

issues.title: Loop sign and ranges: negative feedback depends on the external plant; supplies are fine
issues.detail: Error = setpoint - photodiode (U7), then U9 inverts, IVC102 inverts, and U11 inverts again, so VControl = +(Kp + Ki/s)(SP - PD). The VCA810 (if used) is non-inverting. This is negative feedback only if increasing J11 raises the light on the photodiode. The AD8429 (+/-4.5 to 18 V), OPA189, OP177, LF356, IVC102, DG303A (30 V total), MAX876 (10 V from 15 V) and LDK320 (2.5-18 V) are all within +/-15 V rails. The MAX876 10 V reference sets the setpoint range, (the MAX876 output has no local capacitor drawn; check its datasheet). VCA810 gain-control polarity is 0 V = -40 dB, -2 V = +40 dB.
issues.evidence: U7 net: R1/U1.7 to U7.2, R3 from U7.6 to U7.2, R2/R4 divider to U7.3. U9.2 via R5 from /ErrorSignal; U11 summing with R7, R8, R10.
issues.fix: Confirm the AOM driver polarity once with a scope (step the setpoint) and write the polarity on the board; no schematic change needed.

issues.title: Photodiode input has no bias return and no protection
issues.detail: J2 connects the two AD8429 inputs with no resistors to ground and no series protection. If the photodiode amplifier output is floating relative to this board's ground the input bias current will drive the amplifier to a rail; the AD8429 inputs also only clamp to the +/-15 V rails, so a source above +15 V or an unpowered source can overstress them.
issues.evidence: Net-(J2-Pin_1): J2.1, U1.4[+]; Net-(J2-Pin_2): J2.2, U1.1[-]; no other component on these nets; U1.6 Ref on GND; R13 = 1M gain resistor (G = 1 + 6k/1M).
issues.fix: Add 1M bias-return resistors to ground and 1k series resistors with diode clamps if the source is not guaranteed to be within the rails.

name: Magnetic Noise Cancellation (magnetometer PID lock with coil-control output)
status_note: Fully routed 4-layer board (silkscreen: V1.0, Weiss Group @ Penn State, Peng Du, 01/25/2023) with no unrouted nets, but no evidence it was built or tested; the schematic is one day newer than the PCB.
description: This is NOT the 60 Hz notch/phase-shift filter chain suggested by the LTspice 'Line Field Correction' files, and nothing on it connects to mains. It is a feedback (PID) controller for a compensation coil. Three magnetometer axes (Bx, By, Bz) plus two coil-current signals (Ix, I_DC) enter through unity-gain AMP03 difference amplifiers (U1-U5). Off-board potentiometers (J7-J9, J10, J26) set how much of each is added in the inverting summer U8, together with a DC offset from a MAX876 reference (U6) buffered by U7. The sum goes through an analog switch U11 (error or ground, set by Dig1) to become the error signal. That error feeds a proportional stage (U13 with a rheostat on J15), an integrator (IVC102, U14, hold/clear/integrate set by Dig2 and Dig3) and a derivative stage (U19), which are summed by U16. The result optionally passes through a VCA810 gain stage (U17, gain from J14), then U15 sums it with the coil-current input I_x and outputs a control voltage on J18 'Coil Connection' for an external coil driver; U18 makes a monitor copy on J22. Power is +15 V / GND / -15 V on J6; on-board regulators make +5 V (U9) and -5 V (U10) for the VCA810 and the DG419 logic supply.

issues.title: U16 output (up to about ±13 V) drives VCA810 powered from ±5 V
issues.detail: The VCA810 +In pin is connected straight to the output of U16, an OP177 on ±15 V, through no resistor or clamp, while the VCA810 runs from ±5 V. A large error (integrator wind-up, sensor saturation, startup) can drive the input well beyond its supply rails and damage it (I recall the abs max input as the supply voltage; not verified). Even in normal use, gain up to +40 dB on a signal of a few hundred mV will clip to about ±3.5 V.
issues.fix: Add a series resistor (about 1 kΩ) plus clamp diodes to the ±5 V rails (or fast Schottkys) at U17.1, and limit U16 swing. Check the VCA810 absolute-maximum input in the datasheet.

issues.title: Proportional stage U13 is open loop if J15 is unplugged
issues.detail: The only feedback path of U13 is the off-board rheostat on J15 (pin 1 = output, pin 2 = inverting input). With the connector empty or the rheostat open, U13 has no feedback and its output rails to about ±13 V, which goes through R12 into the sum and on to the coil control output. A pot set to 0 Ω instead gives zero proportional gain, which is safe.
issues.evidence: J15.1 on /V_p (U13.6 output, R12.2); J15.2 on Net-(J15-Pin_2) (R10.1, U13.2 [-]). No other component connects U13.2 to U13.6.
issues.fix: Add a fixed feedback resistor in parallel with J15 (e.g. 100 kΩ), or a series resistor, so U13 always has a defined gain; document the rheostat wiring on the silkscreen.

issues.title: No local decoupling at the VCA810 supply pins
issues.detail: The only +5 V and -5 V capacitors are C18 (1 µF) and C19 (100 nF) at the regulators, about 40 mm from U17. The VCA810 is a wideband (tens of MHz) amplifier that needs capacitors right at +VS and -VS, otherwise it can oscillate or pick up noise that ends up in the coil-control signal.
issues.evidence: +5V net caps: C18 only (placed at x=166,y=91 mm); -5V net caps: C19 only (x=172,y=98 mm). U17 is at x=208,y=111 mm.
issues.fix: Add 100 nF in parallel with 1-2.2 µF at U17 pins 6 and 7 to GND, as close as possible.

issues.title: J6 power pinout is symmetric: a reversed plug swaps ±15 V
issues.detail: J6 is a 3-pin Molex KK with +15 V, GND, -15 V in that order, so a plug inserted backwards swaps the rails exactly. There is no reverse-polarity or fuse protection, and 19 ICs plus the regulators would see reversed supplies.
issues.evidence: J6.1=+15V, J6.2=GND, J6.3=-15V; no diodes or fuses on the +15V / -15V nets; no keying text on silkscreen (only the title text).
issues.fix: Use a keyed/locking connector with a different pin order, or add series Schottky diodes/PTC fuses on both rails; label the pins on the silkscreen.

issues.title: U9 is drawn with a 5.5 V regulator symbol but takes +15 V in
issues.detail: U9 is fed from +15 V. The part named in the schematic, LDK320M50R, is rated for 18 V operating and 20 V absolute maximum, so it is within its limits. The library symbol used is a TPS7A05, which is a 5.5 V part; fitting that or a similar low-voltage LDO would destroy it. The LDO also drops 10 V, so it runs warm above a few tens of mA.
issues.evidence: +15V net includes U9.1 (IN) and U9.3 (EN); value LDK320M50R; symbol TPS7A0531PDBV. LDK320 ratings from the ST datasheet DS11321 (looked up).
issues.fix: Keep the LDK320M50R and correct the symbol. Check that U9 is not hot on the built board.

issues.title: R17 and R18 are either/or links but both are drawn as fitted
issues.detail: R17 bypasses the VCA810 gain stage and R18 takes its output; the schematic note says the gain stage may not be necessary. Both are 0 Ω with no do-not-fit mark. With both fitted, the VCA810 output is shorted to its own input and to U16's output.
issues.evidence: R17: 0 Ω, pin1 /V_cntrl, pin2 Net-(U17-+In) which also holds U16.6 and U17.1. R18: 0 Ω, pin1 Net-(U17-VOUT)=U17.5, pin2 /V_cntrl. /V_cntrl also feeds R11 (to U15) and R19 (to U18).
issues.fix: Fit only one. Check which is fitted on the built board and mark the other as not fitted in the schematic.

issues.title: Digital control inputs have no pull resistors or protection
issues.detail: Dig1 goes to the DG419 IN pin and Dig2/Dig3 go to the IVC102 S1/S2 pins directly from 2-pin connectors. With the cable unplugged these float, so the error switch and the integrator mode (hold/clear/integrate) are undefined at power-up, which could wind the integrator and kick the coil output.
issues.evidence: /Dig1: J13.2, U11.6 [IN]. /Dig2: J12.2, U14.11 [S1]. /Dig3: J11.2, U14.12 [S2]. No resistors on these nets; tracks 0.254 mm.
issues.fix: Add pull-down (or pull-up, matching the safe state) resistors of 10 kΩ and a 1 kΩ series resistor on each input; document the logic truth table on the board.

issues.title: U15 (OP177) is the coil-control output, with no series resistor
issues.detail: J18 is labelled 'Coil Connection' and is driven directly from the OP177 output (about ±10 mA capability) with only a 1 nF feedback cap. If J18 goes to the external coil driver input this is fine, but if a real coil or a long cable is attached the op amp will current-limit, and a cable capacitance can destabilise it. The silk text in the schematic says 'Current control for X coil', so it is most likely a control voltage, which is why this is minor. There is no sense resistor or flyback arrangement because the power stage is not on this board.
issues.evidence: Net-(J18-Pin_2) = U15.6 [output], C25.2, J18.2; U15.2 net has R11 (1 kΩ), R15 (1 kΩ), C25 (1 nF).
issues.fix: Add about 100 Ω in series at U15.6 outside the feedback loop (or inside with a feedback cap), and label J18 as 'to coil driver input, not to a coil'.

issues.title: Pot weights and offset are one polarity only
issues.detail: The pots on J7-J9 (and the fixed 50k for Bx) can only scale each sensor between 0 and 1, and the 10 V reference (U6) only gives one sign of offset. Sensor signs must therefore be set by swapping the input leads, and the offset can only be subtracted, not added, at the summer U8 output. Not a fault, but it is easy to get a positive feedback sign wrong.
issues.evidence: R2/R4/R5/R6/R7/R8/R9 all 50k into U8.2; J10.1 = U6.6 (positive reference), U7 buffer into R8.
issues.fix: Document the intended sign of each input on the silkscreen, or add an inverter option; consider a bipolar offset (reference through +/- selection).

issues.title: Mismatch with the LTspice line-field simulations and brief
issues.detail: The LTspice files model a mains-fed 170 V divider (120k/6.8k), zener clippers (BZX84-A2V4), notch/phase stages and an OPA549 current stage with a 260 µH coil and 1 Ω sense. None of this is on this board: there is no mains input, no notch or phase filters, no power stage. The KiCad board is a magnetometer-based PID lock, so nothing on it needs mains isolation. The mains-related issues (divider ratings, clamping, isolation) should be assessed against the LTspice concept or a different board, not this one.
issues.evidence: Components list: only AMP03, OP177, IVC102, VCA810, MAX876, DG419 and regulators; sims reference V1 SINE(0 170 60), R1 120k/R2 6.8k, OPA549, L1 260µ.
issues.fix: If a line-synchronous feedforward board exists elsewhere, review it separately; otherwise rename the folder/title so that it is not confused with the notch-filter concept.

issues.title: Loop dynamics computed from the actual values
issues.detail: Integrator (U14): total capacitance = 10 nF (C28) + 10+30+100 pF internal = about 10.14 nF (the schematic note says 1000 pF built in, which is out of date), so unity-gain frequency = 1/(2π·R_J17·10.14 nF), e.g. about 1.6 kHz for 10 kΩ. Derivative (U19): input corner 1/(2π·1 kΩ·10 nF) = 15.9 kHz; feedback pole = 1/(2π·(R22 + R_J24)·10 nF), e.g. about 16 kHz at R_J24 = 0, 1.6 kHz at 9 kΩ. U15/U18 feedback poles: 1/(2π·1 kΩ·1 nF) = 159 kHz. Proportional gain = R_J15 / 1 kΩ. The 60 Hz range is all well inside these bandwidths, but the actual rheostat values decide the loop gain and stability; the board gives no limit on them.
issues.evidence: C28 10 nF, C36 10 nF, C38 10 nF, R21 1k, R22 1k, R10 1k, C25/C33 1 nF, R11/R15/R19/R20 1k; rheostat values J15/J17/J24 are unknown.
issues.fix: Record the intended rheostat values and the target loop crossover on the schematic; consider a minimum series resistor with each rheostat.

issues.title: Reference U6 (MAX876) has no output capacitor; offset reference is 10 V
issues.detail: I believe the MAX876 is the 10 V member of the MAX872-876 family (datasheet link is in the schematic); this needs about 12.5 V+ input so the 15 V rail is enough but not by much. The only nearby capacitor is C_REF1 100 nF on the +15 V input, nothing on the output, and the output goes through a cable to an off-board pot. Check the datasheet for the required output capacitor; COMP/TRIM/TEMP are left open, which is allowed.
issues.evidence: U6.2 on +15V with C_REF1; U6.6 only on J10.1; U6.8, U6.5, U6.3, U6.1, U6.7 unconnected.
issues.fix: Add the datasheet-recommended output capacitor next to U6.6 and a COMP noise capacitor if low noise matters.

name: Bias Coil Driver - OPA549 power stage (High Current board)
status_note: A 101.6 x 50.8 mm board exists, but the April 2024 schematic was changed after the board (Ref/ILIM re-tied to V-, status LED added) and the board was never updated, so the two disagree.
description: This is the high-current output stage for a magnetic bias coil. An OPA549T power op amp (U1) takes a control voltage on J2 (IN), has its inverting input brought out on J2 (Feedback), and its output goes to the coil through the J1 terminal block (OUT, +V, -V supply on the same block). The op amp is used with external feedback: the Feedback pin is meant to be wired to a sense or follower connection made off-board, and a four-terminal shunt resistor (R1/J3, GND2) is provided for measuring coil current. The E/S pin of the OPA549 (enable and thermal-shutdown status) is brought to J2 and, in the newer schematic, drives a 74LVC1GU04 inverter and an LED. Supply is a separate high-current dual supply (+VDC / -VDC), decoupled with 10 µF electrolytic plus 0.1 µF ceramic per rail. Signal ground (GND) and shunt/power ground (GND2) are separate copper pours on the board.

issues.title: Board does not match the April 2024 schematic
issues.detail: The schematic (Apr 2024) ties OPA549 Ref (pin 6) to V- and ILIM (pin 8) to Ref through a 0 Ω resistor, and adds an inverter, LED, 330 Ω and extra decoupling. The board still has pins 6 and 8 on the GND pour, no ILIM resistor footprint, no LED/inverter, and the shunt pins on net names that differ from the schematic. If boards are ordered from the .kicad_pcb, E/S levels and the Ref/ILIM behaviour are the old (GND-referenced) ones, not the documented ones.

issues.title: No flyback clamp or snubber for the inductive coil
issues.detail: The coil connects to J1 OUT with nothing on the board to catch the inductive kick. If the supply drops, the enable is pulled, or thermal shutdown trips while the coil carries amps, the coil current keeps flowing into the OPA549 output and drives it beyond the rails. The OPA549 datasheet recommends external clamp diodes from the output to the supplies for inductive loads (recalled from the datasheet, not re-checked online).
issues.evidence: Net /Out has only J1.1 and U1.1, U1.2; no diodes on the board or schematic; no footprint pads for a diode pair or an RC snubber.
issues.fix: Add footprints for two fast, high-current Schottky diodes (Out to +VDC and -VDC to Out), and optionally a series RC snubber from Out to ground and a feedback capacitor option.

issues.title: No thermal provision for the OPA549 on the board
issues.detail: HS1 is a TO-220 heatsink footprint that is not attached to any net and sits about 56 mm away from U1, so it does nothing for the OPA549. A power op amp driving a low-resistance coil from ±15 V dissipates tens of watts (for example 5 A with 5 V across the coil and 10 V across the op amp gives 50 W), far more than a TV5G-size heatsink can remove. The OPA549 tab is at V-, so an external heatsink also needs an insulating pad.
issues.evidence: HS1 Heatsink_Aavid-TV5G_TO220_Horizontal at (196.85, 73.0) with no net; U1 at (140.8, 85.3) with two unconnected mounting pads at ±12.7 mm; no thermal pour or mounting note on silkscreen.
issues.fix: Decide and document the heatsink (large heatsink or fan, insulated from V-), add mounting holes matching it, and calculate dissipation from the actual coil resistance and supply.

issues.title: Status inverter has no defined supply in the schematic
issues.detail: The 74LVC1GU04 that drives the status LED has its ground pin on V−. Its VCC node has only capacitors on it: the wire toward the GND symbol stops short, and the 5 V regulator that the Full version has here is missing. If VCC were wired straight to GND, the part would see the whole negative rail (15 V at ±15 V), above its 6.5 V limit. The board does not include this inverter at all.
issues.evidence: U?.3 (GND) on -VDC; U?.5 (VCC) is on no net with a source; in the schematic image the VCC wire ends before the GND / 0.33 µF node. DRC: footprint for U? missing from the board.
issues.fix: Add a regulator that makes V− + 5 V for the inverter (as in the Full schematic, with its pins corrected) before adding this to the board.

issues.title: Supply decoupling and power return go through the signal connector
issues.detail: The J1 power block carries only OUT, +V and -V; the 0 V (GND) used by all four decoupling capacitors and the Ref/ILIM tie exists only on J2 pin 4, the 4-pin KK 254 signal connector. The high-frequency current loop of the output stage and the signal ground therefore share a thin wire, and GND and GND2 are separate pours that must be tied together somewhere off-board. This is not documented on the silkscreen.
issues.evidence: C1-C4 pad 1 on GND, pad 2 on +VDC/-VDC; GND appears on J2.4 only; GND2 on J3.4 and R1.4 only; no net tie between GND and GND2 on the board.
issues.fix: Add a GND pin to J1 (or a heavy GND terminal), place the 10 µF capacitors close to U1 supply pins with a short return to the power ground, and document or add a single deliberate GND-to-GND2 tie point.

issues.title: Current limit is disabled and not selectable on the board
issues.detail: The schematic's 0 Ω ILIM-to-Ref link disables the OPA549 current limit, leaving only thermal shutdown to protect against a shorted coil or loop fault. On the board, ILIM is hard-wired to the same GND net as Ref. There is no way to fit a limiting resistor without cutting copper.
issues.evidence: Board U1 pads 6 and 8 both on GND; schematic R? 0Ω between ILIM and V-/Ref; note text 'To disable the current limit, short ILim to Ref'.
issues.fix: Provide a footprint for the ILIM resistor and pick a value from the OPA549 datasheet ILIM table for the coil's maximum safe current.

issues.title: E/S status on J2 is referenced to V-, not to the GND on J2
issues.detail: Per the schematic note, E/S in shutdown sits at Ref + 3.5 V and enabling or disabling is relative to Ref, which is now V-. J2 offers E/S next to a pin labelled GND (0 V). A logic card connected there would see about -11.5 V in shutdown at ±15 V and cannot disable the output with a 0 V pull-down.
issues.evidence: J2.1 on /E/S with U1.9; J2.4 on GND; Ref (U1.6) on -VDC in the schematic.
issues.fix: Do not connect J2 pin 1 to external logic without a level shifter or optocoupler, and label the pin accordingly.

issues.title: Sense resistor is a placeholder with no value or power rating
issues.detail: R1 uses a 4-terminal terminal-block footprint and J3 duplicates the same footprint wired pad-for-pad in parallel, so the board has two blocks for one shunt. The shunt value is not stated; at 8 A even 0.1 Ω dissipates 6.4 W, which the part and any mounting have to handle. Track widths look adequate: 3.81 mm 1 oz copper on +VDC, -VDC, OUT and the shunt path is about 15 to 20 °C rise at 8 A, but only on the top layer and with 1.8 mm pads on U1.

issues.title: No compensation provision for the inductive-load feedback loop
issues.detail: The inverting input is only a wire to J2; no pads for a feedback capacitor, snubber across the load, or series input resistor exist. With a long cable to a coil and the loop closed through an external sense path, stability depends entirely on how it is wired off-board.

name: Bias Coil Driver Full - signal summing plus OPA549 current servo (2024)
status_note: No board exists; this is the newest and most complete version (Full002 is the older 2022 copy of the same sheet), but the OPA549 block is unannotated and has no footprints.
description: This circuit turns voltages from the timing system (coarse, fine, AC-correction and DC-correction coax inputs) into a controlled current through a magnetic bias coil. Four AMP03 difference amplifiers buffer the inputs, resistor dividers scale them, and an OP177 (U5) sums them with the shunt voltage into an integrator (only a 0.1 µF capacitor in the feedback). The integrator output is the input of the OPA549 power op amp, which is wired as a unity-gain follower driving the coil (L1) in series with a four-terminal shunt resistor R13 to ground. The shunt voltage (pin 3 via 20 kΩ) is fed back to the OP177, so the current, not the voltage, follows the input. Small-signal parts run from ±15 V; the OPA549 has its own +VDC/-VDC high-current supply with Ref tied to V-, and a 78L05 plus 74LVC1GU04 and LED show the OPA549 enable/thermal status. An AD586 5 V reference and potentiometer connector J4 can replace the coarse input for the EDM/BEC experiments, and J8 is a coax output of the shunt voltage.

issues.title: Integrator can wind up to the rail and slam the coil
issues.detail: U5 has only C10 (0.1 µF) from output to inverting input and no resistor, so it has infinite DC gain and no clamp. If the coil or shunt sense wire is disconnected, the OPA549 is disabled or in thermal shutdown, or the OPA549 saturates, U5 integrates up to its rail. When the fault clears, the OPA549 follows to nearly full supply and drives the coil from 0 Ω-ILIM (limit disabled) until the loop catches up, limited only by coil resistance and thermal shutdown.
issues.evidence: Net-(U5--): C10.2, R6/R7/R8/R12.1, R9.1, U5.2; /In: C10.1, U5.6 and OPA549 +IN; shunt pin 3 via R9 (20 kΩ) is the only feedback; ILIM tied to Ref by R? 0 Ω.
issues.fix: Add a back-to-back diode clamp (or bipolar limit) across C10 and a large DC resistor in parallel with it if drift allows, and set the OPA549 current limit via the ILIM resistor. Consider tying the enable to hold the integrator in reset.

issues.title: No flyback clamp or snubber across the coil
issues.detail: L1 connects between the OPA549 output and the shunt with no clamp diodes or RC network. When the supply collapses or the output is disabled while the coil carries current, the inductive kick pushes the output past the rails, which the OPA549 datasheet advises protecting against with external clamp diodes (recalled, not re-checked online).
issues.evidence: Net /Feedback: L1.2, OPA549 pins 1, 2, 3; Net-(L1-Pad1): L1.1, R13.4; no diodes in the netlist besides the LED.
issues.fix: Add Schottky clamp diodes from OUT to +VDC and -VDC, and optionally an RC snubber across the coil connection.

issues.title: OPA549 current limit disabled and no thermal or SOA note
issues.detail: R? 0 Ω ties ILIM to Ref, which disables the current limit; with ±VDC up to ±30 V and a low-resistance coil, protection is only thermal shutdown. No heatsink part is drawn (the earlier board's HS1 is absent here) and dissipation at the working current is not documented.
issues.evidence: R? 0Ω between ILIM (U?.8) and -VDC; note 'To disable the current limit, short ILim to Ref'; no heatsink or power note.
issues.fix: Choose an ILIM resistor for the maximum safe coil current and document supply voltage, coil resistance and heatsink for the stated current (OPA549 is 8 A continuous).

issues.title: Regulator symbol pin names are reversed versus the real part
issues.detail: U? LM78L05ACZX is drawn with VI on pin 1 and VO on pin 3, but the TO-92 78L05 is pin 1 = output, 2 = GND, 3 = input (recalled, not checked online). The schematic wires pin 3 (named VO) to 0 V and pin 1 (named VI) to the logic rail, which is correct for the real TO-92 pinout but looks backwards and triggers an ERC power-output conflict. The assigned footprint, TO-220-3 vertical, has the opposite pin order (1 = input, 3 = output), so the part would be wired backwards if built from that footprint.
issues.evidence: Net GND: J2.2 [power_out] and U?.3 [VO|power_out]; -VDC: U?.2 [GND] (regulator GND); ERC pin_to_pin: Power output and Power output. Schematic PDF: VI to the inverter VCC node, VO to GND.
issues.fix: Fix the symbol so names match the TO-92 pin numbers, assign a TO-92 footprint, and check that |V-| is at least about 8 V for the regulator to hold 5 V.

issues.title: Shunt sense wiring flaw documented by the designer
issues.detail: A schematic note says the shunt is wired so that the coil current has two paths to ground and the sense is not a true four-terminal measurement; EDM and BEC boxes use an untested workaround (summing-board ground as shunt ground). The coil return also shares the summing-board GND reference with all signal grounds.
issues.evidence: R13 pins: 1 GND, 2 U5.+ (Net-(U5-+)), 3 J8.In and R9, 4 L1.1; text note 'The current design is a mistake'.
issues.fix: Take pin 2 of R13 and R9's return as a Kelvin pair to the OP177 inputs and make one single star ground point at shunt pin 1.

issues.title: AMP03 REF pins left unconnected on all four input stages
issues.detail: U2, U3, U4 and U6 have pin 1 (REF) floating. On the AMP03 this node normally goes to ground; leaving it open changes the gain of the positive-input path and reduces rejection of ground differences between the coax shield and the board ground.
issues.evidence: unconnected-(U2-REF-Pad1), (U3-REF-Pad1), (U4-REF-Pad1), (U6-REF-Pad1); ERC pin_not_connected x4.
issues.fix: Connect REF to the same ground as the shield input, or confirm with the AMP03 datasheet that open is acceptable.

issues.title: Divider ratios differ from the note and sign is inverted
issues.detail: The note says the Fine and Ext Correction inputs divide by 0.01. R2/R4 (10 kΩ/100 Ω) gives about 0.0099, but R3/R5 and R10/R11 (3.9 kΩ/100 Ω) give about 0.025 for the AC and DC correction inputs. Also, the summing integrator is inverting, so a positive input produces a negative shunt voltage and current out of the OPA549 is negative.
issues.fix: Update the note to the actual ratios and add the current-per-volt formula (depends on R13).

issues.fix: Annotate and assign footprints before layout.
