name: Summing Circuit V5 (bias coil driver signal summing / servo front end)
status_note: Newest and most complete version: 50.8 x 50.8 mm four-layer board with no unrouted nets in DRC; git commit and BOM/paste-file outputs suggest it was sent for build, but nothing in the files proves it was assembled. Supersedes Bias Coil Driver / V3 / V4.
description: This board takes the lab's control voltages and turns them into one command for the OPA549 bias-coil driver. Four differential inputs (Coarse from Supertime or an optional 5 V AD586 reference plus pot, Fine Tuning, AC Correction, DC Correction) each go through an AMP03 unity-gain difference amplifier (U2, U3, U4, U6). Coarse gets a low-pass (R1 4.7k with C9 30 nF); the other three are heavily divided down (about 1/100 to 1/500) so they act as small trims or feed-forward corrections. All four are summed through resistors (R6, R7, R8, R12) into the inverting node of an OP177 (U5), which has only a 0.1 µF capacitor (C10) as feedback, so it is an integrator. The coil/shunt voltage returns through R9 (20k) on J3 'From Coil' and U5's non-inverting input goes to 'From Shunt Ground', so U5 integrates until the shunt voltage matches the summed setpoint, and its output goes to the OPA549 board over J3 pin 3. Supplies are ±15 V on J2, each IC has 0.1 µF on both rails.

issues.title: U5 is a pure integrator: output winds to the rail if the loop opens
issues.detail: C10 (0.1 µF) is the only feedback element between U5 output and the inverting node; there is no resistor across it and no clamp. With J3 unplugged, the OPA549 board unpowered/disabled, or the driver current-limiting, U5 integrates any setpoint or its own offset until it hits about ±13 V and then drives the OPA549 input hard when the loop closes again (wind-up, large coil current step). Even with zero input, OP177 offset alone moves the output at roughly tens of mV per second, so an unplugged board slowly creeps to a rail.
issues.evidence: Net-(U5--): C10.2, R6.1, R7.1, R8.1, R9.1, R12.1, U5.2; /To OPA549: C10.1, U5.6, J3.3; R9 = 20k, C10 = 0.1µF. Loop unity-gain frequency of the R9 path = 1/(2π·20k·0.1µ) ≈ 80 Hz, coarse path time constant 47k·0.1µ ≈ 4.7 ms. In the full driver (prep/Bias Coil Driver Full002) U5.6 feeds U7 OPA549 +IN directly.
issues.fix: Add a clamp or limit on the U5 output (series resistor plus back-to-back zeners, or a 'loop enable' switch/relay that shorts C10 when the coil driver is disabled), and power the OPA549 board before or with this board. A large resistor across C10 (about 1 to 10 MΩ) would stop creep but adds a small DC error, so decide against the required current accuracy.

issues.title: R3 and R10 differ between schematic (50k) and BOM/board (3.9k)
issues.detail: The AC and DC correction divider resistors R3 and R10 are 50kΩ in the schematic (saved 2022-09-14) but 3.9kΩ in the BOM csv (2022-09-05) and in the board footprint values (KiCad DRC flags both as symbol/footprint value mismatches). The two values change the correction gain by about a factor of 12.5, so whatever was built or will be built may not match the documented sensitivity.
issues.evidence: Schematic: R3 = R10 = 50kΩ. Summing Circuit V5.csv: R3 = R10 = 3.9kΩ. DRC [footprint_symbol_mismatch] for R3 and R10 (symbol value 3.9kΩ). With R5/R11 = 100Ω and R8/R12 = 50k to the summing node, gain from AC or DC SIG to the shunt-voltage setpoint (through R9 20k) = 20k·100/(R·100+R·50k+5M): 50k gives about 8.0e-4, 3.9k gives about 1.0e-2. For comparison Fine (R2 = 10k) gives 4.0e-3 and Coarse 0.387.
issues.fix: Decide which divider is intended, make schematic, BOM and footprint values agree, and check the populated resistors on any built board.

issues.title: Gain notes on the schematic do not match the actual path gains
issues.detail: The page says the Fine and Ext Correction dividers give 'Vout = 0.01 * Vin'. Computing from the real values the divider ratios (R4/(R2+R4) etc.) are 0.0099 for Fine, 0.002 for the 50k AC/DC channels (0.025 with 3.9k), and each path then still passes through a 50k resistor into the integrator, so the setpoint gain relative to Coarse is about 0.010 (Fine), 0.002 (AC/DC at 50k) or 0.026 (AC/DC at 3.9k). R5 is also stated as 29.9Ω on the x axis board, so the AC channel gain differs per axis. The Coarse low-pass is quoted as 1100 Hz but with U5's 47k load it is about 1.24 kHz.
issues.evidence: AMP03 pins: SIG on -IN (pin 2), GND on +IN (pin 3), REF (pin 1) to GND, SENSE tied to OUT, so each AMP03 inverts (Vout = GND_x - SIG_x) and U5 inverts again. Coarse path: R1 4.7k + R6 47k = 51.7k, C9 30 nF; corner = 1/(2π·(4.7k||47k)·30n) ≈ 1.24 kHz. Fine path equivalent resistance 5.06 MΩ, AC/DC (50k) 25.1 MΩ.
issues.fix: Update the notes on the schematic with the real numbers (setpoint-to-shunt-voltage gain per channel) and the per-axis R5 value so that the Supertime scaling can be set correctly.

issues.title: U5 non-inverting input is only grounded through the interboard cable
issues.detail: U5.3 connects only to /From Shunt Ground (J3.2); the board has no local path from that net to GND. If J3 is unplugged or the shunt-ground wire is broken, the OP177 input floats and its output drifts to a rail. Also, the AMP03 stages are referenced to board GND (J2.2) while U5's reference is the shunt ground, so any IR drop between the two is injected into the loop as an offset (about 0.39 times the ground difference through the Coarse path). The git history notes that earlier versions tied U5.3 to GND, which this revision fixed.
issues.evidence: /From Shunt Ground: J3.2[power_out], U5.3[+|input]; GND net: U2.1, U3.1, U4.1, U6.1 (REF pins), J2.2. ERC [pin_to_pin] error is only the J3 symbol being typed 'power output' on a signal pin.
issues.fix: Add a DNP 0Ω or high-value resistor footprint from /From Shunt Ground to GND for bench use, and connect the shunt-ground wire close to the point where the coil current returns so the ground offset is small.

issues.title: OP177 output drives the interboard cable directly
issues.detail: U5.6 goes straight to J3.3 and onto a cable to the OPA549 board with no series isolation resistor. A cable's capacitance on an op amp output reduces phase margin; because the 0.1 µF feedback capacitor sits on the output side, adding a resistor inside the loop is awkward, so a ~100Ω resistor after the C10 tap is preferable.
issues.evidence: /To OPA549: C10.1, J3.3, U5.6; no resistor between U5.6 and J3.3 in the nets file. Cable length is not specified.
issues.fix: Add a 50 to 100Ω series resistor between the C10 tap and J3.3 (C10 stays on the op amp side); keep cable short or check for oscillation with a scope.

issues.title: Coarse input net is shared by J1 and the pot wiper on J4
issues.detail: The AD586 5 V reference drives J4.1 only; the pot wiper (J4.2) is wired onto the same /SIG_Coarse net as J1.2 and the AMP03 input. The board silk says 'Optional, replaces J1', so if both a pot and the NI/Supertime signal are connected the pot wiper fights a low-impedance analog output. Pot value is not given anywhere and the AD586 output has no series resistor, so a shorted pot cable loads the reference.
issues.evidence: /SIG_Coarse: J1.2, J4.2, U2.2; /Vin_RV: J4.1, U1.6; J4.3 on GND; W1 (0Ω) ties GND_Coarse to GND.
issues.fix: Leave J1 unplugged when the pot is used (or add a jumper/switch), specify a pot value (about 5k to 10k like the 2019 design) and add 100 to 200Ω in series with J4.1.

issues.title: No input protection or series resistance on external connectors
issues.detail: J1, J6, J7, J8 bring NI analog outputs and other lab signals directly to AMP03 inputs. The AMP03 input resistors (about 25 kΩ per input, from datasheet memory) limit fault current, and signals are ±10 V against ±15 V supplies, so risk is low, but nothing protects against a connector being plugged into a supply line or a powered-off board being driven by an active AO.
issues.evidence: /SIG_Coarse, /SIG_Fine Tuning, /SIG_AC Correction, /SIG_DC Correction go to U2.2, U3.2, U4.2, U6.2 only; no clamp diodes or series resistors in nets file. NI AO load = about 25 kΩ differential, well within PCI-6713/6733 drive.
issues.fix: Optional: 1k series resistor plus a clamp, or at least label connector polarity; the main safeguard is not hot-plugging.

issues.title: No offset trim and no bulk supply capacitor
issues.detail: U5 offset pins (1 and 8) are left open and AD586 TRIM is open, so setpoint accuracy depends on OP177 and AMP03 offsets; at the AC/DC channel gains of about 1e-3 the full-scale correction is only a few mV on the shunt, so offsets of tens of µV are visible. The only supply capacitors are 0.1 µF per IC (C2 to C14), with no 10 µF at the J2 power connector (the 2019 design mentions 10 µF tantalums at the supply inputs).
issues.evidence: unconnected-(U5-VOS-Pad1), unconnected-(U5-VOS-Pad8), unconnected-(U1-TRIM-Pad5); +15V: C2,C3,C5,C7,C11,C13 (all 0.1µF); -15V: C4,C6,C8,C12,C14.
issues.fix: Add an optional OP177 null pot (per datasheet) or DNP footprint, and a 10 µF capacitor on each rail at J2.

issues.title: Layout and labelling notes
issues.detail: Board has all nets routed (no unconnected or clearance items in DRC); GND zone on In1.Cu, +15V and -15V on 0.635 mm tracks, signals on 0.25 mm. Silkscreen title still reads 'Summing Circuit V2', and the AC/DC labels on the board are swapped for U4/U6 (the schematic documents this as 'Note 2'). name: Simple summing circuit for AO847 (2019)
status_note: Legacy 2019 drawing by T.-Y. Wu; the .sch is not readable plain text (binary/obfuscated header 'xV1'), so it was reviewed from the .bmp; it is a separate, earlier concept from the bias-coil summing board.
description: A two-input non-inverting summer built around an LF356 that adds a manual 0 to 5 V offset to the Supertime control voltage before it goes to the 847 nm acousto-optic modulator's external control inputs. The offset comes from an AD586 5 V reference and a 5k pot, and both it and Vin go through 10k resistors to the op-amp's non-inverting input, with a 10k/10k feedback pair giving a gain of 2, so Vout = Vin + Vpot. issues.fix: Add a termination (for example 10k to GND at the Vin side, or a switch/jumper) so an open input reads as 0 V, or limit the output with a clamp.

issues.title: No output isolation or range limit into the AO control box

name: Active Twin-T notch filter (tunable, bootstrapped)
status_note: Schematic and a routed 38.1 x 31.7 mm board exist (silkscreen 'NOTCH FILTER V1'), but there is no gerber/BOM in the folder to show it was fabricated, and the component values are still symbolic (R, C, 2*C).
description: A one-channel notch filter for removing a single mains harmonic (60, 180 or 300 Hz) from an analog signal. The signal enters on J1 pin 3, goes through a twin-T network (two series resistors plus a shunt capacitor, in parallel with two series capacitors plus a shunt resistor), and is read by op-amp U1A wired as a unity-gain follower; the result leaves on J2. A second op-amp, U1B, buffers a fraction of the output (set by potentiometer RV1) and drives the grounded ends of the twin-T shunt legs ('bootstrapping'), which raises the notch Q. Power is +/-15 V on J1 with a 100 nF capacitor per rail. The notch frequency is set by the resistors and capacitors, f0 = 1/(2*pi*R*C), and R3, R6 and R1 are off-board trim resistors. LTspice files with the same name use R = 53.1 kOhm, C = 10 nF (f0 = 299.7 Hz) and R = 27 kOhm, C = 100 nF (f0 = 59 Hz).

issues.title: Notch depth needs R and C matched to ~0.1-0.3 percent
issues.detail: A twin-T only nulls when the series legs are R, R, the shunt leg is R/2, the capacitors are C, C and the shunt capacitor is 2C. I simulated the board topology at f0 = 300 Hz (R 53.1k, C 10n) with random tolerance on all six elements and the notch re-centred: passive (RV1 at ground) typical depth is -57 dB at 10 percent, -65 dB at 1 percent, -76 dB at 0.1 percent; with the bootstrap at Q = 12.5 (k = 0.98) it falls to -24 dB at 10 percent, -32 dB at 1 percent, -42 dB at 0.1 percent; at Q = 50 (k = 0.995) it is only -10 dB at 10 percent, -20 dB at 1 percent, -29 dB at 0.1 percent. Depth therefore collapses as Q goes up, and the notch frequency itself shifts by roughly the tolerance.
issues.evidence: Nets: C3, C4 series to U1.3; R3+R4 and R5+R6 series In to U1.3; C5 (2*C) from node C5.2 to U1B output; R1+R2 from C3/C4 midpoint to U1B output. Simulation done on exactly this connectivity, Q from sim matches 1/(4(1-k)).
issues.fix: Use 1 percent (or better) C0G/film capacitors and 0.1 percent resistors for the fixed parts, keep the three trim resistors (R3, R6, R1) and tune for depth with a signal generator; for a -40 dB notch at Q >= 10 expect to need 0.2-0.3 percent matched parts plus trimming. State the target depth and Q before buying parts.

issues.title: Symbolic values are inconsistent: R2 = R cannot give R/2 shunt leg
issues.detail: The shunt resistor leg is R1 (R_Variable/2) in series with R2 (labelled R), which sums to more than R, not R/2. Likewise each series leg is a trim (R3 or R6) in series with a fixed R (R4 or R5), so the fixed part must be about 0.85-0.9 of R, not R. Built with R in every fixed position the notch will be at the wrong frequency and cannot be tuned back with the trim ranges implied. 2*C for C5 is also not a value; E-series has no exact 2C so it must be built from parallel parts.
issues.evidence: R2, R4, R5 value 'R'; R1 'R_Variable/2'; R3, R6 'R_Variable'; C3, C4 'C'; C5 '2*C' (nets.txt components list).
issues.fix: Pick the target f0, then fix each part: R4 = R5 = about 0.9 R, R3/R6 trim about 0.2 R centred; R2 = about 0.4 R, R1 trim about 0.2 R; C5 = two C in parallel (or the nearest film value with R1+R2 adjusted).

issues.title: Bootstrap pot at full travel drives the filter to Q = infinity / oscillation
issues.detail: RV1 is a plain potentiometer from /Out to GND with its wiper feeding U1B. At the top end the bootstrap fraction k reaches 1, where Q = 1/(4(1-k)) goes to infinity and real component mismatch can move the poles into the right half plane, so the board rings or oscillates near f0. Q also changes extremely quickly over the last 1-2 percent of rotation (k 0.98 to 0.995 changes Q from 12.5 to 50), which makes tuning touchy.
issues.evidence: RV1.3 on /Out, RV1.2 on Net-(U1B-+) (U1.5), RV1.1 on GND. LTspice 'Active Twin T Filter.asc' uses fixed Rb and N*Rb, N = 50, i.e. k fixed near 0.98, not a free pot.
issues.fix: Put a fixed resistor in series between /Out and RV1.3 (and optionally a series resistor to ground) so the wiper cannot exceed k of about 0.99, and use a multi-turn pot. Specify the RV1 value (10 kOhm is fine).

issues.title: Tuning resistors sit off-board on 2-pin headers at high-impedance nodes
issues.detail: R1, R3 and R6 (and RV1) are Molex KK-254 header footprints for external pots on 50 kOhm-class nodes. The leads act as antennas, and this board exists to remove mains pickup, so 60 Hz coupling into the very node U1A reads (R6 is wired directly to U1.3) can limit the achievable depth. Pot wiper contact noise and drift also move the notch.
issues.evidence: Footprints for R1, R3, R6: Connector_Molex:Molex_KK-254_AE-6410-02A_1x02; RV1: ..._03A_1x03; R6.1 on U1.3 net Net-(U1A-+).
issues.fix: Keep trim leads short and twisted, or use on-board multi-turn trimmers (e.g. Bourns 3296) for R1, R3, R6; enclose the board in a grounded shield box.

issues.title: Bootstrap buffer drives the 2C capacitor directly
issues.detail: U1B output (U1.7, tied to U1.6) connects straight to C5 (2C = 20 nF for the 300 Hz design, about 200 nF for 60 Hz) and to the R1/R2 leg. A unity-gain follower driving a large capacitor can ring or oscillate, and this one also sits inside a positive-feedback loop through RV1. I did not check the AD8676 capacitive-load curve.
issues.fix: Add 10-47 Ohm in series with C5 (negligible against 27-53 kOhm) and check the step response with a scope before trusting a high-Q setting; confirm in the AD8676 datasheet.

issues.title: No protection/series resistor on connectors; supply decoupling is far from U1
issues.detail: J1 (+15V, -15V, In, GND in pins 1-4) has no reverse-polarity protection and the input has no clamp; U1A drives J2 and cable capacitance directly. The only supply decoupling is one 100 nF 1206 per rail placed about 24 mm from U1 on 0.25 mm traces, with no bulk capacitor, which is poor for a 10 MHz GBW op amp. The connector pin names are not on the silkscreen.
issues.evidence: C1 (127.7,110.2) and C2 to U1 (146.8,124.2) = about 24 mm; track width 0.25 mm all nets; only silk text is 'NOTCH FILTER V1 ...'; J2.1 = /Out directly.
issues.fix: Add 100 nF at U1 pins 4 and 8, a 10 uF per rail, a 47-100 Ohm series output resistor, and label J1/J2 pin functions on the silkscreen.

issues.title: ERC/DRC triage: no real electrical or manufacturing errors
issues.detail: ERC: 13 warnings, all library symbol mismatch / not found in library (power symbols, Conn_01x0x_Male). DRC: 15 lib_footprint_mismatch (local footprint overrides) and 9 'net_conflict' parity items; I checked each conflict and they are name-only (pad net 'Net-(C4-Pad2)' vs schematic 'Net-(U1A-+)', 'Net-(C5-Pad1)' vs 'Net-(U1B--)', 'Net-(RV1-Pad2)' vs 'Net-(U1B-+)') with identical pin membership. 0 unconnected pads, no clearance errors. U1 pin mapping matches the AD8676 SOIC-8 pinout (1 OUTA, 2 -INA, 3 +INA, 4 V-, 5 +INB, 6 -INB, 7 OUTB, 8 V+).

name: Second Order Phase Shifter (two cascaded all-pass stages)
status_note: Routed 38.1 x 21.0 mm board ('PHASE SHIFTER V1') exists but values are generic and nothing shows it was fabricated; the LTspice 'Line Field Correction Phase Stage.asc' holds the intended values.
description: A tunable phase shifter used to line up the phase of a mains-frequency signal (60 Hz and harmonics) before it is summed into a noise-cancelling field coil. Two identical all-pass sections are cascaded: each is an AD8676 op amp with equal resistors from the input and from the output to the inverting pin, and a variable resistor plus capacitor to ground at the non-inverting pin. Each section passes all frequencies at gain 1 and shifts phase by -2*atan(2*pi*f*R*C); two sections give -4*atan(2*pi*f*R*C), from 0 to -360 degrees. The signal enters J1 pin 3, goes through U1A then U1B and leaves on J2. Supplies are +/-15 V on J1 with one 100 nF per rail. The simulation uses R1=R2=R4=R5=10 kOhm, C = 2 uF and trim R = 1.33 kOhm, which gives exactly 180 degrees at 60 Hz.

issues.title: Phase accuracy and drift depend on 1206 capacitors that cannot be good enough
issues.detail: For the 60 Hz design (C = 2 uF, R = 1.33 kOhm, f*R*C = 1) the total phase changes by about 1.15 degrees for every 1 percent change in R*C (4*x/(1+x^2) rad per unit relative change at x = 1). A 2.2 uF X7R 1206 is +/-10-20 percent, has a large voltage and temperature coefficient and microphonics, so phase will be off by 10 degrees or more until trimmed and will drift with room temperature. A phase error of 1 degree limits cancellation of the interfering tone to about -35 dB. Film capacitors of this size will not fit the 1206 pads.
issues.evidence: C3, C4 value 'C', footprint Capacitor_SMD:C_1206_3216Metric; R3, R6 R_Variable (KK-254 headers); LTspice: C1 = C2 = 2u, Rs = 1.33k, ac sweep 59-61 Hz.
issues.fix: Use through-hole film (PET/PP) or parallel C0G capacitors via a different footprint for C3 and C4, or switch to a smaller C with larger R (the pots then need to be 10-30 kOhm). Trim R3 and R6 against a scope at the operating frequency and re-check after warm-up.

issues.title: Low input impedance loads the source and varies with frequency
issues.detail: With the simulation values J1 pin 3 drives R1 (10 kOhm) in parallel with R3 + C3, which is about 1.6-1.9 kOhm at 60 Hz and falls to about 1.2 kOhm at high frequency. A weak source (or a long lead from a DDS or filter) will be loaded, and its source resistance adds to R3 and shifts the phase.
issues.fix: Drive it from an op-amp output (below about 50 Ohm), or raise all resistors by 10x and lower C by 10x.

issues.title: Resistor pairs must match for unity gain; no trim ranges defined
issues.detail: Each stage is only an all-pass with gain exactly 1 if R1 = R2 and R4 = R5; a mismatch of e percent gives a gain error of about e percent at high frequency versus DC, and a cascade of two. R3 and R6 are bare symbols 'R_Variable' on 2-pin headers with no value, so the tuning range is undefined (C tolerance of 20 percent needs at least +/-25 percent range).
issues.evidence: R1, R2, R4, R5 'R' on 1206; R3, R6 R_Variable footprint Molex_KK-254_AE-6410-02A.
issues.fix: Use 0.1 percent resistors for R1/R2 and R4/R5; specify a 2 kOhm multi-turn trimmer for R3 and R6 (for C = 2 uF).

issues.title: No input protection, no output series resistor, decoupling far from op amp
issues.detail: J1 and J2 go straight to the op amps with no clamps or isolation, and U1B drives J2 and any cable directly. The 100 nF supply capacitors are about 24 mm from U1 on 0.25 mm traces and there is no bulk capacitor. J1 pin functions are not on the silkscreen.
issues.evidence: C1 (123.19,106.68) to U1 (147.32,106.43) about 24 mm; J2.1 on /Out = U1.7; silk text only 'PHASE SHIFTER V1 ...'.

status_note: Mostly a block-diagram sketch: text boxes for the stages, one drawn phase stage and one OPA549 block, nothing annotated (all refs are '?') and no PCB (empty .kicad_pcb).

name: 5 Stage Butterworth Bandpass Filter (six Sallen-Key bandpass sections)
status_note: Schematic only (empty .kicad_pcb), no footprints on any R/C, all values are the placeholders R and C, and the wiring has errors (see issues).
description: A planned high-order bandpass filter for picking out one mains harmonic, built from six identical second-order bandpass sections in series, using three dual AD8676 op amps (U1A to U3B). The signal enters J1 pin 1, each section is a resistor into a node with a capacitor pair and a resistor to ground, then a non-inverting op amp with a resistor-pair gain setting; the output of the last section is meant to go to J1 pin 2. Power is +/-15 V on J1 pins 5 and 6 with a capacitor pair on each IC. No component has a value, so the centre frequency, Q and gain cannot be computed from the file.

issues.title: Each section feeds its output back to its own + input: DC latch-up
issues.detail: In every section, R3 (stage 1) connects the op amp output to the non-inverting input, while the inverting input has a 1+R4/R5 gain divider. With positive feedback fraction 1 and negative feedback fraction 1/K (K = 1+R4/R5 > 1), the node equation gives a real right-half-plane pole at s = (K-1)/(R3*C8); the stage cannot be stable and will sit at a supply rail. Even with K = 1 the section reduces to a plain divider and does no filtering. The intended Sallen-Key bandpass has this resistor returned to ground, not to the output.
issues.evidence: Net-(U1A-+): C8.2, R3.1, U1.3; Net-(C7-Pad2): C7.2, R3.2, R4.2, R6.1, U1.1. Same pattern in U1B (R8 to U1.7 net), U2A (R13 to U2.1), U3A (R23), U3B (R28).
issues.fix: Move the second terminal of R3, R8, R13, R18, R23, R28 to GND (check against the intended Sallen-Key bandpass topology), then simulate the whole chain in LTspice before building.

issues.title: Stage-4 (U2B) feedback network is disconnected from its output
issues.detail: C13.2 and R18.2 sit on their own net with no op-amp pin, while U2B's output (U2.7) is on a different net with R19 and R21. So U2B's non-inverting input (U2.5) only has C14 and an open-ended R18: it has no DC path and floats, and the stage 4 shape is wrong. The wire geometry matches this: there is no vertical wire at x = 185.42 mm above y = 90.17 mm to join the feedback line to the output.
issues.fix: Add the missing wire joining C13.2/R18.2 to U2.7 (the same way the other five sections are drawn), re-run ERC and check there are no single-pin nets.

issues.title: Filter output is never connected to J1 OUT
issues.detail: The label OUT beside J1 pin 2 is dangling and the output of the last stage (U3.7) has a wire stub with nothing on it, so the filtered signal is not available on the connector. Net /OUT contains only J1.2.
issues.evidence: /OUT : J1.2 only. ERC: label_dangling 'OUT' at (88.90,35.56); unconnected_wire_endpoint at (261.62,90.17).
issues.fix: Wire U3 pin 7 (Net-(C17-Pad2)) to J1.2 /OUT, preferably through a 50-100 Ohm series resistor.

issues.title: Title says 5 stage but six sections are drawn; values/order undefined
issues.detail: Three AD8676 duals give six second-order sections (12th order), not five; a Butterworth response needs each section tuned to a different Q and centre/edge frequency, while the schematic uses the same placeholders R and C in every position, so as drawn all sections would be identical (a stagger-less cascade, not Butterworth). The 'bandpass' also has no stated centre frequency (60/180/300/420 Hz?).

name: VCA810 voltage-controlled amplifier
status_note: Complete schematic and routed 34x25 mm two-layer board (silk 'VCA V1 05/2023'); no evidence it was built or revised.
description: A small variable-gain amplifier board built around the TI VCA810 (-40 dB to +40 dB, linear-in-dB gain, ±5 V supplies). A signal comes in on J3 (pin 1 signal, pin 2 ground) to the VCA810 non-inverting input (the inverting input is grounded) and leaves on J4 from the VOUT pin. A gain control voltage on J2 goes straight to the VCA810 gain pin with no scaling. The board takes ±15 V on J1 and makes its own +5 V (LDK320M50R LDO from +15 V) and -5 V (LM79L05 from -15 V) for the VCA810. Everything is DC coupled and the back copper layer is a ground pour.

issues.title: Gain pin has no scaling, so lab AO levels will not work
issues.detail: VCA810 gain is G(dB) = -40*(Vc+1), valid only for Vc between 0 V (+40 dB) and -2 V (-40 dB); Vc must be kept above about -2.5 V, and a positive Vc of 0.15 V or more shuts the amplifier off. J2.1 goes directly to U1.3 with nothing in between, so a normal 0 to +10 V or ±10 V analog output will either mute the amp or push the pin far below -2.5 V. The control law is also inverted relative to the usual 'more volts = more gain'.
issues.evidence: Nets /GC: J2.1 and U1.3 only; no resistors anywhere on the board (only C1,C2,CR1-CR4 and connectors). Datasheet (TI SBOS275G, looked up on the web) gives pin 3 gain control, 0 to -2 V span, 2 V disable, -2.5 V limit.
issues.fix: Add an input stage: an inverting op amp or divider that maps the driving voltage (e.g. 0 to +10 V) to 0 to -2 V, plus a clamp (series resistor and Schottky diodes or a limiting amp) so pin 3 can never go below -2.5 V. Document the polarity on the silkscreen.

issues.title: No protection on any connector pin of a ±5 V-supplied part
issues.detail: The VCA810 absolute maximum for input and common-mode voltage is ±Vs (±5 V on this board) and its pins have ESD diodes to both rails. J3 (In) and J2 (Gain) are plugged into cables from ±10 V lab equipment with no series resistor, clamp or termination; a ±10 V signal or a mis-set analog output would forward-bias the ESD diodes and can damage the part. The gain pin also bleeds current into -5 V if driven negative past about -5.5 V, which could back-feed the LM79L05.
issues.evidence: J3.1 -> U1.1 (+In) direct; J2.1 -> U1.3 direct; J4.1 <- U1.5 direct. No R, D or TVS on the board. Datasheet abs max: input and CM voltage ±VS.
issues.fix: Add a series resistor (about 1 k to 10 k) and a pair of Schottky or low-leakage clamp diodes to the ±5 V rails on /In and /GC, and a small series output resistor (about 50 Ω) on /Out. Consider label silkscreen 'max ±1.8 V in'.

issues.title: Gain input floats when J2 is unplugged
issues.detail: /GC has no pull resistor. With J2 disconnected (or the source at power-up) the control pin floats; the VCA810 gain pin has 6 µA bias current so it can drift anywhere from disabled to +40 dB gain, possibly giving a large unexpected output on whatever is on J4.
issues.evidence: /GC only connects J2.1 and U1.3; no pull-down or pull-up.
issues.fix: Add a divider or a pull-up to a small positive voltage (e.g. toward +0.15 V or more via resistors) so the default state is muted, or a pull to a known mid gain value, and keep source impedance below 100 Ω as TI recommends.

issues.title: Input range is only about ±1 V at high gain, not the ±10 V lab level
issues.detail: The VCA810 swings about ±1.7 V at the output and its usable input shrinks as gain rises (max input is at -40 dB). Connecting this board between ±10 V lab signals will clip badly; at +40 dB a 20 mV input already reaches full scale. The schematic does not state the intended signal levels.
issues.evidence: Supplies +5V (U3.5 -> U1.6) and -5V (U2.1 -> U1.7); U1.1 input and U1.5 output direct to connectors.
issues.fix: Confirm the intended signal level. For ±10 V use, add input attenuation and an output stage; otherwise label the board for small signals only.

issues.title: Power connector pin order differs from the Isolation Amplifier board
issues.detail: J1 on this board is pin1 +15V, pin2 GND, pin3 -15V; the Isolation Amplifier board (same 'Power x3' KK connector) is pin1 -15V, pin2 GND, pin3 +15V. A cable moved between the two boards applies ±15 V reversed, and neither board has reverse protection; here -15 V would hit the LDK320 input and +15 V the LM79L05 input, both of which can be damaged.
issues.evidence: VCA nets: +15V J1.1, -15V J1.3. Isolation Amplifier nets: -15V J1.1, +15V J1.3. No diodes or fuses. J1 silkscreen carries no pin labels (only the title text).
issues.fix: Standardise the pinout across all lab boards, add silkscreen pin labels (+15, GND, -15), and add a series Schottky or polarity-keyed connector.

issues.title: Very little decoupling at the VCA810; shared ground pour under signal pins
issues.detail: Only CR3 1 µF (+5V) and CR1 100 nF (-5V) are on the supplies, placed about 7 mm and 8 mm from U1 on the right side; TI wants 0.1 µF within 6 mm of the pins plus 2.2-6.8 µF bulk. The same datasheet says to open windows in ground planes around signal pins and put >25 Ω in series with ground-referenced input pins; here -In goes straight to ground and a continuous B.Cu GND pour runs under the part. Risk is oscillation or peaking at high gain.
issues.evidence: CR3 at (177.2,107.3), CR1 at (177.2,102.2), U1 at (170.2,102.9). U1.8 (-In) on GND. B.Cu zone net GND, one filled polygon. Datasheet layout guidelines (web).
issues.fix: Add a 100 nF ceramic across each ±5 V pin at the package, keep 1 µF/10 µF nearby, put ~25-50 Ω in the -In ground leg, and cut the ground pour away under the I/O pins.

issues.title: Regulator dissipation and 1206 ceramic voltage rating are unverified
issues.detail: U3 drops 10 V and U2 about 10 V; with roughly 30 mA of VCA810 supply current this is about 0.3 W each in SOT-23-5 and SOIC-8, giving a roughly 50-75 C rise. C1 and C2 (10 µF) and CR2 (1 µF) sit on ±15 V; 1206 10 µF parts are often only 10-16 V rated. A symbol mismatch also exists: U3 uses the TPS7A0531 symbol and datasheet link while the value is LDK320M50R (pinout agrees).
issues.evidence: U3 IN (+15V) to OUT (+5V); U2 IN (-15V) to OUT (-5V); C1 and C2 10µF on +15V and -15V; U3 lib part TPS7A0531PDBV.
issues.fix: Check VCA810 supply current for the actual use, use 25 V rated X7R for C1, C2, CR2, CR4, and fix the U3 symbol/datasheet link.

name: 'Isolation Amplifier' (actually AMP03 difference amplifier)
status_note: Schematic and routed 25x19 mm board exist (silk 'ISOLATION AMP May 2023'); the part used is not an isolation device, so the board does not do what its name says.
description: Despite the name, this board is a unity-gain precision difference amplifier built on the Analog Devices AMP03 (SOIC-8). The two input pins on J2 go to the AMP03 inputs (J2.1 to +IN, J2.2 to -IN) and the output on J3 pin 1 is the difference between them referred to ground; J3 pin 2 and the AMP03 REFERENCE pin are ground. It runs from ±15 V on J1 with 100 nF decoupling on each rail. It can be used to remove ground-loop offsets on a signal, but it gives no galvanic isolation.

issues.title: Not galvanically isolated: it is a difference amplifier
issues.detail: The board is labelled ISOLATION AMP, but U1 is an AMP03 unity-gain difference amplifier with one ground and one pair of supplies. It breaks ground loops by rejecting common-mode voltage within its input range. It gives no safety isolation and no protection beyond that range.
issues.evidence: U1 AMP03GSZ: V+ (U1.7) on +15V, V- (U1.4) on -15V, REFERENCE (U1.1) and J3.2 on GND; J2 has no ground pin at all. PCB: one zone net GND on B.Cu; pad-to-pad creepage under the SOIC is just the standard 0.6 mm-wide pad pitch (1.27 mm centres). Pinout AMP03 SOIC-8 (1 REF, 2 -IN, 3 +IN, 4 V-, 5 SENSE, 6 OUT, 7 V+, 8 NC) confirmed via web search of the datasheet.
issues.fix: Rename it (differential receiver or ground-loop breaker). Do not use it where true isolation is needed.

issues.title: No input protection; abs-max input vs ±10 V lab signals unverified
issues.detail: J2 connects straight to U1.2 and U1.3 with no series resistor, clamp or filter, and the board has no ground on J2 to shield the cable. The datasheet input common-mode range (a distributor lists ±20 V, not confirmed in the datasheet text) is wide, but a fault such as the signal pair being connected to a supply or a transient on a long cable has nothing to limit it. The output on J3.1 drives the cable directly with no series resistor.
issues.evidence: J2.1 -> U1.3 (+IN), J2.2 -> U1.2 (-IN); J3.1 <- U1.5/U1.6 direct. No R/D on board.
issues.fix: Add 1 k to 10 k series resistors (check against noise/CMRR) and a clamp to the rails on both inputs, and a 50-100 Ω series output resistor.

issues.title: Power connector pin order differs from the VCA board
issues.detail: J1 here is pin1 -15V, pin2 GND, pin3 +15V; the VCA board's identical 'Power x3' KK connector is pin1 +15V, pin2 GND, pin3 -15V. Swapping a power lead between the boards reverses the rails on the AMP03 and can destroy it; there is no reverse protection and no pin labels on silkscreen.
issues.evidence: Nets: -15V J1.1, GND J1.2, +15V J1.3 (Isolation Amplifier); VCA: +15V J1.1, -15V J1.3. Silk text only the title.
issues.fix: Standardise the pinout across all lab boards, add silkscreen pin labels and series diodes or a keyed connector.

issues.title: Fixed gain of 1; input range limited by supplies
issues.detail: Gain is fixed by the internal resistors (SENSE tied to OUTPUT, REFERENCE to GND), so there is no gain setting at all. Output swing is limited to a few volts inside the ±15 V rails, which matters if the source is ±10 V with common-mode offset (the difference input subtracts but the internal divider can clip first). Confirm the intended use.
issues.evidence: U1.5 and U1.6 on one net with J3.1; U1.1 on GND.
